jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Reporting to the VP Finance, the Director, Finance [East] provides financial leadership and strategic business partnership. The role is accountable for the integrity of financial reporting, operational performance analysis, cost accounting, financial planning and internal controls, while driving continuous improvement and supporting informed business decisions.

Working closely with Operations and cross-functional leaders, the Director translates financial and operational results into actionable insights, identifies opportunities to improve performance, and drives accountability for the timely resolution of issues.

This role is also responsible for leading and developing a team 13 finance professionals (direct and indirect reports), building a culture of ownership, collaboration, continuous improvement and strong financial discipline across the operations.

Key Responsibilities

Leads change, challenging assumptions and the status quo to demonstrate and instill a continuous improvement mindset
Leads teams in a decentralized organization structure, taking individual initiative to engage others and translate business goals into plans, priorities and individual performance measures
Delegates projects with clear set of agreed objectives / measures of success and timelines (taking corrective action when necessary, including escalation of issues)
Strategic business partner providing professional insight into all aspects of the operations from procurement and inventory control to business development
Preparation and distribution of monthly financial reports to management including analysis of monthly divisional and facility results (daily, weekly, monthly) and ad-hoc analyses as required
Develops a result-oriented finance team that drives financial performance / productivity and acts as an information service provider ensuring appropriate leadership and guidance is provided to the various stakeholders, including enhanced reporting and timely, insightful, action-oriented variance analysis
Recommends and oversees implementation of approved capital expenditure process supporting investment decisions and required ROI (return on investments)
Maintenance of control processes to ensure responsible working capital management and efficient use of company resources
Monitoring and oversight of the divisions internal control processes and coordination with the company's auditors to ensure efficient review and audit execution

Requirements

CPA Professional Accounting Designation (developed in and focused on Operations Finance)
Experience (15 yrs.), including 10 years in directly related, leadership & people management roles
Experience in manufacturing - food preferred
Plant Controller experience is required
Strong understanding of yield accounting, labour analysis and inventory master costing / modelling
Resilient, focused leadership skills demonstrated under pressure
Team / People management and development skills to attract, coach, grow and maximize talent
Strong communication skills on both technical as well as non-technical matters; strong written and verbal presentation skills
Conflict resolution and negotiation skills
Ability to work in fast paced environment, with prioritization, process engineering and people management skills to ensure attention to detail and quality is maintained
Ability to multi-task with multiple deadlines and prioritize crucial deliverables
Excellent time management skills (ability to multitask and manage deadlines and multiple customer demands)
Experience implementing and maintaining ERPs (AS400 desirable)
Exceptional skills in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Power Point and Outlook)

Job Posting Range

Hiring Range: CAD $120,100 - $170,100
Bonus: This position is eligible for a bonus up to 17.5% of base salary subject to the plan terms and conditions.
Please note that the expected hiring range provided is derived from a group of like roles within Sofina. The final offer amount for this role will be dependent on geographical region, applicable experience, skillset of the candidate and internal equity.

jobs.title: Vice-President, Finance and Operations
jobs.description:
The University of British Columbia (UBC) is one of the world’s leading research universities—an institution inspiring people, ideas and actions for a better world. With two main campuses in Vancouver and the Okanagan, more than 73,000 students, over 20,000 faculty and staff, 25,000 full-time campus residents, over 435,000 alumni, and an annual consolidated budget over $4 billion, UBC combines global reach with a deep commitment to Canada, British Columbia and the communities it serves.

UBC’s academic excellence and societal impact are driven by a research community attracting close to $1 billion in annual funding, and supported by extraordinary assets including extensive physical infrastructure, a $3.5 billion endowment fund, and a full range of services that sustain vibrant learning, working and living environments. UBC’s Strategic Directions 2025–2030set an ambitious course for discovery, partnership, emerging technologies and collaboration across its two distinct and complementary campuses, and reaffirms UBC’s long-standing commitments to reconciliation, inclusion and sustainability.

UBC is seeking a strategic and collaborative Vice-President, Finance and Operations to align financial and operational capacity with its academic and research ambitions. The VPFO will provide integrated leadership for financial strategy and stewardship, financial planning and analysis, treasury, financial operations, facilities and infrastructure, capital investment, safety, risk and assurance, while supporting the long-term value of the university’s physical and financial assets. This is a significant opportunity to help shape the future successes of one of the leading research institutions in Canada and globally.

A trusted partner to the entire UBC Community - including the President and executive team, Board of Governors, Host Nations, Deans and senior leaders, student leaders, campus residents and alumni community - the VPFO will translate institutional priorities into sustainable multi-year financial and operating strategies in service of the University’s academic mission. Working collegially across faculties, campuses and administrative units, the Vice-President will strengthen planning, resource allocation and risk-informed decision-making, and lead modernization of systems, processes and services. The role calls for a leader who builds and engages strong teams, communicates complex choices clearly, has successfully demonstrated change in a complex environment, and balances institutional consistency with the needs of a distributed academic environment.

The ideal candidate brings executive-level experience with responsibility for finance and significant operational functions in an organization of comparable scale, complexity and public accountability. Experience in a large Canadian research-intensive university is strongly preferred; leaders from other highly complex sectors will also be considered. Candidates will demonstrate strategic financial depth, operational breadth, sound governance and a track record of leading enterprise-wide change with integrity and transparency. A sustained commitment to reconciliation, inclusion and sustainability is essential. A university degree is required; a relevant graduate degree, CPA designation, or other relevant financial designations are highly desirable. A combination of equivalent senior leadership experience and education credentials will be considered.

To explore this exceptional opportunity further, please contact our Search Consultants at Boyden at ubc@boyden.com or click Apply to submit your resume.

At UBC, we believe that a diverse workforce contributes to the pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning. We encourage applications from marginalized groups based on the grounds enumerated under the B.C. Human Rights Code. All applicants will be asked to complete a confidential diversity survey. If you have any accommodation or accessibility needs during the job application process, please contact the Centre for Workplace Accessibility at workplace.accessibility@ubc.ca.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. We thank all applicants for their interest in this position. Please note that we will only be in contact with those individuals moving forward within this search. In accordance with BC’s Pay Transparency Act, the position has an expected base salary range of $340,000 - $380,000.

Position Description

The Opportunity

Toronto Financial Services is entering its next phase of growth. Artificial intelligence is changing how clients operate, Global Capability Centres are reshaping delivery models, and market disruption is accelerating. Clients increasingly look to CGI for strategic business outcomes.

CGI is investing in a leader who can accelerate growth, strengthen executive relationships, expand consulting-led engagements, and position CGI as a partner for business and technology transformation.

You will bring together CGI’s capabilities—including Business Consulting, Systems Integration, Managed Services, AI-enabled services, reusable IP, and strategic partnerships—to solve clients’ business challenges and build long-term relationships.

As leader of one of CGI Canada’s largest Financial Services businesses, you will have full accountability for growth, profitability, client relationships, delivery excellence, and leadership development. You will grow the business by connecting clients with the full breadth of CGI’s capabilities.

Your future duties and responsibilities

What you’ll deliver

Accelerate growth

Grow organically and win new business across Managed Services, Systems Integration, Business Consulting, and IP—in existing client ecosystems and new markets.

Elevate Business Consulting

Make Business Consulting a primary driver of transformational engagements. Build consulting-led opportunities that create lasting strategic partnerships and deepen CGI’s influence within client organizations.

Drive profitable growth

Improve profitability through disciplined portfolio management, innovative commercial models, and operational excellence. Expand higher-value, outcome-based engagements and strengthen contribution margins.

Build AI into the business

Use AI to improve productivity, delivery, and client outcomes. Develop new revenue opportunities through AI-enabled services.

Build a high-performing culture

Develop a strong leadership bench and attract exceptional talent. Simplify the operating model to support growth without proportional increases in headcount, while fostering energy, collaboration, and belonging.

Create new demand

Raise CGI’s profile with clients, alliance partners, and the market through measurable client outcomes, strategic relationships, and thought leadership.

Grow through partnerships

Work with hyperscaler and technology partners, and pursue client co-innovation, to extend CGI’s reach and create new growth opportunities.

Who you’ll work with

Report to the BU Leader, Financial Services.
Lead Vice Presidents and Directors across Consulting, Delivery, and Client Management.
Partner with enterprise leaders in Business Consulting, IP and AI, HR, Marketing, and Operations.
Build strategic relationships with alliance partners and industry leaders.
Engage directly with C-suite executives across the client base.

The operating code

Own it: Address problems early with accountability and ownership.
Move at the speed of the opportunity: Make timely decisions and respond to clients’ needs.
Bring ideas before they’re asked for: Shape the agenda and anticipate opportunities.
Make AI non-negotiable: Build AI fluency across the leadership team and the business.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

What you’ve done before:

Built or scaled a consulting, technology, or managed services business with full P&L accountability, growing revenue and margin together.
Driven organic growth and new client acquisition across multiple service lines.
Led executive-level client relationships and secured large, strategic engagements, including opportunities developed before formal procurement.
Shifted staff augmentation or time-and-materials engagements to outcome-based commercial models.
Built leadership teams and succession plans, and raised market visibility through analyst relations, media engagement, and industry recognition.

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

jobs.description:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Company Description

Visa is a world leader in payments and technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. Our mission is to connect the world through the most innovative, convenient, reliable and secure payments network, enabling individuals, businesses and economies to thrive.

Make an impact with a purpose-driven industry leader. Join us and experience Life at Visa.

Team Summary

The Canada Strategy & Operations team helps shape how Visa Canada grows and executes against its market priorities. Working closely with Canada market leadership, Sales, Business Lines, Finance and regional teams, the team connects strategy with execution and helps ensure we focus on the opportunities that matter most. The team’s remit spans market and commercial strategy, sales operations, business planning and performance management, with a focus on continuously improving how we serve clients and drive growth.

What a Director, Strategy & Operations does at Visa Canada

The Director, Strategy & Operations is responsible for strengthening commercial strategy, sales effectiveness and operating discipline across the market, serving as a key partner to the sales organization and Canada leadership team. Reporting to the Vice President, Strategy & Operations, the Director will translate Canada’s strategic priorities into commercial action, strengthen performance management, and continuously evolve how we sell as client expectations, competition and technology change.

The role requires someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution, identifying where and how we should grow and translating those opportunities into clear priorities and measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Sales & Commercial Strategy

Translate Canada’s market priorities into clear sales and commercialization strategies.
Support client segmentation, account prioritization and coverage strategy.
Partner with Sales and Business Lines to identify and accelerate priority growth opportunities.
Help evolve Canada’s sales and coverage model as client needs, competition and the payments landscape change.

Commercial Performance & Execution

Own the Canada sales operating rhythm, including forecasting, performance management and business reviews.
Track performance against revenue, payment volume and sales objectives, providing clear, forward-looking insights.
Support the Canada Leadership Team operating rhythm, ensuring discussions are anchored in business performance, strategic priorities, key risks and clear actions.
Identify performance gaps, commercial risks and growth opportunities and drive actions to improve outcomes.
Provide leadership with a clear view of business performance and areas requiring intervention.

Sales Effectiveness & Optimization

Improve how the frontline sells, including account planning, opportunity management, pipeline discipline and CRM adoption.
Strengthen the connection between account plans, commercial opportunities, investments and business outcomes.
Simplify processes, remove friction and increase seller capacity, improving productivity and commercial effectiveness.
Leverage data, automation and AI to strengthen insights, streamline work and enable better client engagement and decision-making.
Partner with regional and global teams to bring relevant tools, capabilities and best practices into Canada.

Strategic Leadership & Partnership

Serve as a trusted thought partner to Canada leadership and account executives.
Bring a fact-based, forward-looking perspective to commercial priorities, investments and resource decisions.
Influence across a highly matrixed organization to translate priorities into action and measurable results.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

10+ years of experience in strategy, sales operations, commercial management, consulting, financial services, payments or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to improve sales effectiveness, operating processes and frontline productivity, including through data, automation and AI.
Strong commercial and financial acumen, with experience in sales planning, forecasting, pipeline management, performance management and/or commercialization.
Experience in payments, banking, fintech or a complex B2B commercial environment preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into execution, turning complex business priorities into clear plans, actions and measurable outcomes.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize financial, client, sales and market data into actionable insights and recommendations.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence across a matrixed organization without direct authority.
Strong executive communication skills, with experience developing and presenting clear recommendations to senior leaders.
High degree of ownership and sound judgment, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Software Engineering – Data Platform
jobs.description:
Passionate about precision medicine and advancing the healthcare industry?

Recent advancements in underlying technology have finally made it possible for AI to impact clinical care in a meaningful way. Tempus' proprietary platform connects an entire ecosystem of real-world evidence to deliver real-time, actionable insights to physicians, providing critical information about the right treatments for the right patients, at the right time.

Passionate about precision medicine and advancing the healthcare industry?

Recent advancements in underlying technology have finally made it possible for AI to impact clinical care in a meaningful way. Tempus' proprietary platform connects an entire ecosystem of real-world evidence to deliver real-time, actionable insights to physicians, providing critical information about the right treatments for the right patients, at the right time.

All of that depends on data moving reliably and at scale: real-time clinical messages streaming in from health systems, petabyte-scale batch backfills, and datasets shared with partners. Data Platform builds the systems that move healthcare data into and out of Tempus, and we are making that platform self-service, so any team at Tempus can ingest, transform, and share data on its own, with data governance built in so every dataset carries the usage rules that apply to it.

We are looking for a Senior Director of Software Engineering to lead our Data Platform engineering organization, set its technical direction, and report to the Chief Data Technology Officer.

The Team

Data Platform Is Organized As Small, Autonomous Pods. Each Pod Owns a Clear System Domain And Partners With a Dedicated Product Manager

Edge Compute: Builds, packages, and operates a fleet of on-premises appliances deployed inside health systems, along with a growing catalog of connectors to on-premises clinical systems for batch and real-time use cases. The pod manages fleet health at scale and is opening the edge so other Tempus teams can deploy their own workloads there.
Gateways & Processing: Runs the high-throughput, secure cloud gateways (FHIR APIs and large-scale file transfer) that partners use to send messages and files, and the processing tools that map, enrich, and validate that data. The goal is that 100% of incoming data is application-ready, standardized FHIR, delivered through integration patterns that serve both people and machines.
Pipeline Orchestration: Builds event-driven pipelines and a workflow orchestration platform with robust error handling, logging, and repair, so clinical workflows run reliably at scale. The pod also owns egress, letting data owners define how their data is packaged and delivered, and tracks every message through its full lifecycle.
Identity & Trust: Lays the foundation for privacy enforcement. The pod masters patient identity across sources, tags data with its allowed usage contexts and enforces them, and maintains centralized audit logging and search for every movement of patient data.

Where We're Going

The Next Generation Of The Platform Moves Well Beyond Ingest And Egress. You Will Set The Strategy And Lead The Teams Building

Edge AI: Running model inference across our fleet of edge appliances, close to where clinical data is generated.
Federated compute: Training machine learning models across institutions around the world without moving the underlying data.
Real-time data delivery: Shifting from scheduled batch deliveries to continuous, low-latency data products.
Multi-hyperscaler architecture: Operating natively across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, meeting partners in the cloud they already use.
Native platform integrations: Delivering data directly into Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, and other data platforms our partners rely on.
Zero-copy architectures: Sharing governed data in place instead of duplicating it across systems and clouds.
Clean rooms: Privacy-preserving environments where researchers can analyze sensitive data under strict controls.

What You'll Do

Lead and grow a multi-pod organization of engineering managers, engineers, and architects. Hire, coach, and develop the next generation of engineering leaders.
Set the technical direction for streaming and batch data pipelines, balancing real-time latency with petabyte-scale throughput.
Turn the vision above into a roadmap, partnering with product, research, and business leaders to sequence investments and deliver them.
Build self-service capabilities that let teams across Tempus ingest, transform, and share data without waiting on engineering.
Build governance into the platform, including identity resolution, usage-based access controls, and auditability for every data flow, including data shared with third parties.
Modernize the platform by consolidating legacy pipelines onto unified, standardized processing.
Raise the bar on reliability, observability, and incident response for systems that carry clinical workflows and protected health information.

How You Lead

You treat pipelines and platform capabilities as products, with clear owners, contracts, and service levels.
You measure success by how much the rest of the company can do with data without filing a ticket with your team.
You give pods real autonomy over their domains while keeping system boundaries and contracts clean across them.
You are technical enough to review an architecture, a distributed data job, or an incident timeline, and you lead through your managers rather than around them.
You write things down. Playbooks, design reviews, and decision records are how the organization scales.
You build strong partnerships with product, data content, security, and the teams that depend on the platform, and you make trade-offs openly.

Experience Requirements

12+ years in software or data engineering, including 5+ years leading teams through managers.
Ownership of production data platforms at multi-petabyte scale, spanning streaming and batch, with SLAs and on-call responsibility.
Hands-on depth with Airflow, Spark, and event-driven messaging systems on a major public cloud.
Experience designing systems that span multiple clouds or migrate large workloads between them.
Experience working with PHI or other regulated data under HIPAA or comparable controls.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Master's degree preferred.

Bonus Points

Healthcare data standards such as HL7 v2 and FHIR, or EHR data.
Identity resolution or master patient index systems.
Edge or on-premises software fleets, including ML inference at the edge.
Federated learning, clean rooms, or other privacy-preserving computation.
Zero-copy data sharing or native integrations with Databricks, Snowflake, or Microsoft Fabric.
Experience at a health-tech, diagnostics, or life-sciences company.

Chicago: $200,000-$270,000

The expected salary range may vary for other locations. Actual salary may vary based on qualifications and experience. Tempus offers a full range of benefits, which may include incentive compensation, restricted stock units, medical and other benefits depending on the position.

jobs.title: Director, Solutions Architecture
jobs.description:
About Coursera + Udemy

Coursera and Udemy are now one company, bringing together two mission-driven brands to create the world’s most powerful platform for turning learning into progress. Together, we help more than 300 million learners and 12,000+ enterprise customers build the skills they need for a world being reshaped by AI. Read more about the combined company by visiting our blog.

Why join us now?

AI is transforming how people learn, work, and grow, and the need for new skills has never been greater. Coursera brings trusted content and credentials from leading university and industry partners, while Udemy brings a dynamic skills marketplace and global network of real-world experts. By combining these strengths, we can connect more people and organizations to the skills they need, when they need them.

Shape What Comes Next

By joining our team, you’ll have the opportunity to reshape how the world learns and applies skills—and help millions of people participate in the new economy. Bring your ideas, expertise, and perspective to meaningful work that can make a difference at global scale.

How We Work

Coursera + Udemy lets you choose the best way to work, whether it’s from home, an office, or a collaboration space. We’re a globally distributed team that comes together intentionally for collaboration, complex problem-solving, and key milestones — creating opportunities for teams to come together. If you’re ready to make a global impact, help scale unique products across Coursera + Udemy, and grow your career, apply below.

Job Overview:

Within Professional Services, you'll lead the Solutions Architecture team through a fundamental change: from a technical intake team that passes integration work to third parties to a team that designs and builds the integrations we choose to own on Workato. You'll decide which integrations are strategic to own and which third parties can deliver faster, and you'll balance capacity across Coursera and Udemy technical work. You'll lay a foundation to build from, so that integrations are productized and reusable rather than one-offs, and you'll upskill the team to design, build, and test the way an engineering team does. You'll also take ownership of integrations built by third parties for both Coursera and Udemy, and decide what, if anything, to migrate in house. This is a highly operational role. You'll redesign how the team works with Product, Partnerships, Presales, and Customer Support, define workflows that are not yet defined, and build the delivery discipline, capacity model, and metrics that make the function run like a well-oiled machine. You'll report to the Senior Director of Professional Services and partner closely with the Director of AI Innovation to streamline how the team works.

Responsibilities:

Lead the shift from a technical intake team that routes work to third parties to a team that builds the integrations we choose to own, and set the criteria, service levels, and pricing for what we own versus what third parties deliver.
Own the integration roadmap and prioritization with Product, Partnerships, Engineering, and Support, and make capacity and load-balancing tradeoffs across Coursera and Udemy technical work.
Establish the Workato foundation and productize what we can, with shared standards and reusable components, and a custom layer on top that is easy to adapt. Build reuse into design review.
Take ownership of the inherited integrations, six years of third-party work on the Coursera platform and a handful on Udemy. Document them, decide what, if anything, to migrate, retire, or keep, and steward the code and its environment.
Hire and upskill the team to design, build, and test like engineers, aligned with Coursera Engineering's standards. Use AI-assisted development deliberately so the team builds fundamentals first, and manage token usage.
Redesign how the team works, including Jira, intake, and workflows with Product, Partnerships, Presales, and Support, and train Support to deflect development-related tickets.
Own the run and support model for what we build, including monitoring, maintenance, versioning, and service levels. Meet security, contractual, and data privacy standards, and serve as the senior escalation point for high-risk issues.
Partner with Presales on early scoping and own the technical handoff from Sales into delivery. Work with the Director of AI Innovation and Solutions on the pilot-to-PS transition review and on streamlining the team's work.
Run utilization and project tracking, manage the technical service catalog, pricing, SOWs, and margin, and build metrics that show impact on deal size, time to production, retention, and quality.

Basic Qualifications:

8+ years of experience in solutions architecture, technical professional services, or integration consulting, with a strong focus on API integrations (REST, SOAP, GraphQL) and cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
Proven experience leading and developing technical teams, ideally globally distributed, and running a technical delivery function, including capacity planning, utilization, and cross-team workflows.
Experience building reusable, productized integrations on an iPaaS platform and designing for reuse across customers.
Experience applying engineering standards (SDLC, design and code review, testing) to integration delivery, and coaching a team to adopt them.
Experience taking over third-party-built or inherited code and making build, buy, partner, and migrate decisions, including managing third-party partners.
Direct experience in pre-sales activity for technical services, including discovery, scoping, and SOW creation.
Strong communicator with stakeholders from engineers to executives. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Job Title

AVP, R&D

Job Description

We have a great opportunity to join our Global R&D function as a leader of a team of five actuaries and analysts. You will be leading the development of biometric assumptions for a range of different global reinsurance markets. We are looking for someone who can influence key stakeholders in the business to maximize the value of assumption knowledge.

In this role, you'll work with colleagues across the company on both Longevity and Protection markets in Europe and North America, giving you diverse exposure and the opportunity to make a real impact. You will be responsible for all aspects of the delivery of assumptions, from planning, team management, technical direction, stakeholder engagement and implementation.

A key focus over the next few years will be to scale the team capabilities for the increase in volume of assumptions which we need to produce. This will come through being courageous in improving economies of scale and standardizing and sharing capabilities.

You will lead stakeholder relationships with people across the business:

R&D teams across multiple geographies
Savings & Retirement and Protection teams inside the Reinsurance Division to support on Pricing and Product developments
Division teams such as Corporate Actuarial, Operations and Risk
Biometric teams in other Divisions on shared assumptions related to the US market

We are a collaborative and friendly team who thrive to provide their best. You will report to the VP, R&D.

How You’ll Help Move Us Forward

You'll be a recognized leader in actuarial assumption development — setting the direction, raising the bar, and leaving a visible mark on how we work across global markets.
Redefine what market-leading looks like. You'll bring genuine intellectual curiosity to assumption development — challenging inherited methodologies, pioneering new analytical approaches, and setting a standard that competitors will follow.
Build a team that scales with ambition. You'll be accountable for growing a high-performing function — streamlining how we work, eliminating inefficiency, and developing the next generation of actuarial talent.
Influence decisions at the highest level. You'll forge strong relationships with senior stakeholders across Pricing, Product, and beyond — translating complex technical judgements into clear, compelling recommendations that drive real business decisions.
Be the function's critical voice. You'll provide rigorous, independent challenge to Pricing assumptions — ensuring intellectual honesty sits at the heart of everything we do.
Shape the profession, not just the company. Through thought leadership, academic partnerships, and research initiatives, you'll help define where actuarial thinking goes next.

Desirable Skills & Experience

Demonstrable exposure to assumption development with a reinsurer, life company or consultancy. This could be through working directly in a pricing or basis setting team or through a review function.
Qualified Fellow of the Institute or Faculty of Actuaries or other similar organisation with 6+ years post qualified experience.
A good understanding of the Longevity insurance/reinsurance market and/or the Protection insurance/reinsurance market.
Ability and desire to come up with and implement new approaches and techniques.
Report writing and verbal communication skills, including ability to present to senior managers and to forge close relationships with other teams.
Ability to think for yourself and challenge the status quo.
Organised and deadline focused.
Interest and understanding of programming and comfortable with or willing to learn software packages, such as Tableau, SQL (or comparable database language) and R.
Experience with people management or mentoring, and interest in coaching and developing junior staff.

jobs.title: Director, International Business Transformation & Strategy Execution (flexible location)
jobs.description:
Chez ABB, nous aidons les industries à être plus efficaces et plus durables, et chaque personne ici contribue à cet impact. Vous aurez le pouvoir d’agir, le soutien nécessaire pour évoluer et la fierté de participer aux résultats que nous créons ensemble. Joignez-vous à nous et contribuez à ce qui fait avancer le monde.

The work model for the role is:
Hybrid

Your Role And Responsibilities

This Director role is a strategic transformation position within ABB's NEMA International division, reporting to the EVP International Sales. The role is pivotal in building a scalable international business platform by strengthening alignment across Regions, Business Lines and functions, removing structural barriers to growth and driving implementation of the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale roadmap. The successful candidate will drive business transformation across regions while building scalable operating foundations, combining expertise in strategy execution, operating-model redesign, business process management, change leadership, and executive influence within a complex global matrix.

The work model for the role is: hybrid ;

The role is contributing to the Motion NEMA Motors division globally.

International travel of approximately 30-40% will be required for the role.

You Will Be Mainly Accountable For

Own and drive the NEMA International transformation roadmap aligned with the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale journey, translating strategy into prioritized initiatives with clear outcomes, milestones and success measures while maintaining visibility of progress and risks to leadership.
Act as senior integrator between NEMA International and Global Business Lines, establishing governance mechanisms and cross-functional commitments that align product, portfolio, and investment priorities with international market requirements while escalating critical dependencies that constrain growth.
Lead resolution of systemic barriers at the interfaces between International Sales, Global Operations, IT, Finance, HR and other supporting functions, converting fragmented issues into prioritized root-cause initiatives with clear accountability and measurable outcomes.
Serve as custodian of the NEMA International target operating model, ensuring organizational accountabilities, governance, processes, technology and capabilities evolve coherently to enable profitable international growth, from stabilization through optimization and scale, while designing the organization for future growth and acquisitions.
Lead an executive-level International Transformation Office that manages the transformation portfolio, governance cadence, dependency view and risk escalation, mobilizing cross-functional workstreams and intervening to resolve ownership gaps, resource constraints or delayed decisions.
Lead adoption of the new international organization and ways of working through change leadership, stakeholder engagement and capability building, while establishing a continuous improvement framework that connects frontline issues to structural business improvements and embeds continuous improvement into leadership accountability.

Qualifications For The Role

Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in business transformation, strategy execution, operating-model design, commercial excellence, enterprise program leadership or management consulting.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Strategy, Operations, Information Systems or a related discipline.
Experience in an internal strategy, transformation, business excellence or consulting role.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation across multiple geographies or business units.
Proven ability to align senior stakeholders and functions behind a shared agenda without relying on direct authority.
Experience translating strategy into executable roadmaps, governance, operating mechanisms and measurable outcomes.
Strong business acumen and ability to connect transformation to customer value, growth, margin, cash, productivity and organizational capability.
Excellent executive communication, facilitation and synthesis skills.
Ability to constructively challenge established practices and navigate ambiguity with pace and judgement.
Familiarity with international commercial models, CRM/ERP environments and end-to-end customer processes.
Experience in an industrial, manufacturing, electromechanical or B2B technology environment is an advantage. Recognized transformation, change management, Lean, Six Sigma or program-management certification is a plus.
Fluent English language skills.

More About Us

ABB’s NEMA Motors Division is a marketer, designer and manufacturer that offers Baldor-Reliance® industrial electric motors, primarily in North America. The Division focuses on quality, reliability and efficiency to provide a comprehensive offering of NEMA motors in the market across most industrial segments and applications.

We value people from different backgrounds. Apply today for your next career step within ABB and visit www.abb.com to learn about the impact of our solutions across the globe. #MyABBStory

We look forward to receiving your application (documents submitted in English are appreciated). If you want to discover more about ABB, take another look at our website
www.abb.com
.

_________________

Directeur(-trice) transformation des activités internationales et exécution de la stratégie (lieu de travail flexible)

Nos convictions

Chez ABB, nous nous engageons à relever les défis mondiaux. Nos valeurs fondamentales — la bienveillance, le courage, la curiosité et la collaboration —combinées à notre engagement envers la diversité, l’inclusion et l’égalité des chances, sont au cœur de notre volonté de donner à chacun et chacune les moyens de créer des solutions durables.

Écrivez le prochain chapitre de votre histoire chez ABB.

Votre rôle et vos responsabilités

Ce poste de direction est axé sur la transformation stratégique au sein de la division NEMA International d’ABB et relève du vice-président exécutif, ventes internationales. Il joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en place d’une plateforme d’affaires internationales évolutive en renforçant l’alignement entre les régions, les secteurs d’activité et les fonctions, en éliminant les obstacles structurels à la croissance et en pilotant la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle. La personne retenue pilotera la transformation des activités dans les différentes régions tout en établissant des fondations opérationnelles évolutives, en mettant à profit son expertise en exécution de la stratégie, en refonte des modèles opérationnels, en gestion des processus d’affaires, en leadership du changement et en influence auprès de la haute direction dans une structure matricielle mondiale complexe.

Le mode de travail pour ce poste est : hybride;

Ce poste contribue aux activités de la division Moteurs NEMA du secteur Motion à l’échelle mondiale.

Ce poste exige des déplacements internationaux représentant environ 30 à 40 % du temps de travail.

Vos Principales Responsabilités Seront Les Suivantes

Prendre en charge et piloter la feuille de route de transformation de NEMA International, en cohérence avec le parcours Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle, en traduisant la stratégie en initiatives prioritaires assorties de résultats, de jalons et de critères de réussite clairs, tout en assurant à la direction une visibilité sur les progrès et les risques.
Agir comme principal point d’intégration entre NEMA International et les secteurs d’activité mondiaux, en établissant des mécanismes de gouvernance et des engagements interfonctionnels qui alignent les priorités en matière de produits, de portefeuille et d’investissements sur les exigences des marchés internationaux, tout en portant à l’attention de la direction les interdépendances critiques qui freinent la croissance.
Piloter la résolution des obstacles systémiques aux interfaces entre les ventes internationales, les opérations mondiales, les TI, les finances, les RH et les autres fonctions de soutien, en regroupant les problèmes isolés en initiatives prioritaires visant leurs causes fondamentales, assorties de responsabilités claires et de résultats mesurables.
Veiller au maintien du modèle opérationnel cible de NEMA International, en s’assurant que les responsabilités organisationnelles, la gouvernance, les processus, les technologies et les capacités évoluent de façon cohérente pour soutenir une croissance internationale rentable, de la stabilisation à l’optimisation, puis au déploiement à grande échelle, tout en concevant l’organisation en fonction de sa croissance et de ses acquisitions futures.
Diriger un bureau de transformation internationale au niveau de la haute direction, responsable du portefeuille de transformation, du rythme de gouvernance, du suivi des interdépendances et du signalement des risques, en mobilisant les chantiers interfonctionnels et en intervenant pour résoudre les lacunes dans l’attribution des responsabilités, les contraintes de ressources ou les retards décisionnels.
Piloter l’adoption de la nouvelle organisation internationale et des nouvelles façons de travailler grâce au leadership du changement, à la mobilisation des parties prenantes et au développement des capacités, tout en établissant un cadre d’amélioration continue qui relie les problèmes de première ligne aux améliorations structurelles des activités et intègre l’amélioration continue aux responsabilités de la direction.

Qualifications Requises Pour Le Poste

Au moins 10 ans d’expérience avec des responsabilités croissantes en transformation des activités, en exécution de la stratégie, en conception de modèles opérationnels, en excellence commerciale, en direction de programmes d’entreprise ou en conseil en gestion.
Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en administration des affaires, en génie, en stratégie, en gestion des opérations, en systèmes d’information ou dans une discipline connexe.
Expérience dans un rôle interne en stratégie, en transformation, en excellence opérationnelle ou en consultation.
Expérience démontrée dans la direction de transformations complexes et interfonctionnelles touchant plusieurs régions géographiques ou unités d’affaires.
Capacité éprouvée à rallier les parties prenantes de la haute direction et les fonctions autour de priorités communes, sans s’appuyer sur une autorité hiérarchique directe.
Expérience dans la traduction de la stratégie en feuilles de route réalisables, en structures de gouvernance, en mécanismes opérationnels et en résultats mesurables.
Solide sens des affaires et capacité à relier la transformation à la valeur pour la clientèle, à la croissance, aux marges, aux flux de trésorerie, à la productivité et aux capacités organisationnelles.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication auprès de la haute direction, en animation et en synthèse.
Capacité à remettre en question les pratiques établies de façon constructive et à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté avec rapidité et discernement.
Connaissance des modèles commerciaux internationaux, des environnements de gestion de la relation client (CRM) et de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), ainsi que des processus clients de bout en bout.
Une expérience dans un environnement industriel, manufacturier, électromécanique ou de technologies interentreprises (B2B) constitue un atout. Une certification reconnue en transformation, en gestion du changement, en Lean, en Six Sigma ou en gestion de programmes constitue un atout.
Maîtrise de l’anglais.

Pour en savoir plus sur nous

La division Moteurs NEMA d’ABB commercialise, conçoit et fabrique des moteurs électriques industriels Baldor-Reliance®, principalement en Amérique du Nord. The Opportunity

Crescent Oral Surgery (COS)
is seeking a dynamic and experienced Practice Director
to join our growing team. This full-time leadership role spans across our three locations in Toronto, Aurora, and Richmond Hill
, and plays a critical part in the ongoing growth and operational excellence of our practices.

Reporting to the Partners
, the Practice Director
will oversee all aspects of day-to-day operations, contribute strategically to our growth initiatives, and lead a team of over 90 professionals. This position will collaborate closely with internal team leads, referral networks, and industry partners, ensuring the delivery of exceptional patient care while driving operational and financial success.

Crescent Oral Surgery
is a leading oral and maxillofacial surgery practice with a strong provincial and national reputation. Our multidisciplinary team of nine Surgeons, two Oral Medicine Specialists, a Radiologist, and a Pain Specialist is dedicated to delivering expert care with professionalism and compassion.

Who You Are

You are a strategic, hands-on healthcare leader who thrives on balancing operational rigour with a genuine commitment to people and patients.
With a proven record in senior leadership, you are equally comfortable owning a P&L, guiding department heads, and building trusted relationships with surgeons, referral partners, and team members.
You lead change with clarity and confidence, bring structure to complex, multi-site environments, and use data to make smart decisions that drive growth.
Collaborative, approachable, and accountable, you inspire high-performing teams and are energized by the opportunity to shape the future of a respected oral surgery practice.

In This Role, You Will

Operational & Financial Excellence

Manage clinic financials, including overseeing profit and loss, revenue forecasting, and labor cost management.
Ensure regular on-site presence at each practice location, to monitor performance and support all staff in delivering high-quality patient care and experiences.
Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews and communicate key metrics to stakeholders.
Collaborate to develop an annual COS budget reflective of the annual growth strategy.
Develop and execute strategies to optimize daily operations across all COS locations.
Oversee procurement processes and coordinate material and resource allocation

Leading People and Building Strong Relationships

Foster a positive, collaborative, and high-performance culture aligned with COS values.
Support associates in building their practices and expanding referral relationships.
Guide goal setting and performance management processes to drive continuous improvement.
Identify talent development opportunities and contribute to succession planning efforts.
Ensure operational alignment between clinical, administrative, coordination, and call center teams through effective team leadership and engagement efforts.
Collaborate with Dentalcorp departments (HR, Compliance, DC Learning) to maintain regulatory compliance and training standards.
Build a strong network and culture across all three practice locations, with Team Leads, Team Members, Associates, Partners, Patients, and the Dental Community at-large as an ambassador for COS.

Patient Care and Experience

Ensure the utmost quality care outcomes for patients, through required compliance training and standards for all COS practices and team members.
Identify, develop, and lead innovative initiatives and improvements to continuously enhance the patient experience, alongside COS Partners and team members.
Work closely with team leads, surgeons, and Dentalcorp support teams to resolve patient concerns and maintain high satisfaction levels.

Transformation and Growth

Develop and oversee the annual growth strategy for COS, including call centre and referral strategy, marketing, talent management, and other growth levers and opportunities
Leverage data insights and identify innovative solutions to drive growth opportunities across all marketing efforts.
Design and implement an annual growth strategy including referral development, marketing, and talent acquisition.
Align strategy with operational implementation to ensure successful outcomes between clinical, admin, and call centre teams across COS practices and community referral practices.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor's and/or Master’s Degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Management or a related field is required.
Proven experience in Senior Leadership Roles, with Advanced Operational and People Management responsibilities is required.
Demonstrated ability to lead change, manage multiple projects, and build strong cross-functional relationships.
Strong strategic thinking, commercial awareness, and execution capabilities.
Strong financial and business acumen, including experience managing P&L, forecasting, budgeting, and performance metrics.
A track record of driving measurable, sustainable growth through operational discipline and KPI management
Excellent leadership, communication, and collaboration skills, with the ability to build strong relationships across functions and levels
Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and executing complex projects with multiple stakeholders
Strong organizational skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively
A valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle, with the flexibility to travel within Ontario, including occasional overnight stays

Why Dentalcorp?

Dentalcorp
is North America’s leading and fastest-growing network of dental practices. Through industry-leading technology, expertise, and scale, we help practices grow while supporting dental professionals to retain their clinical autonomy. Here, you’ll be trusted with meaningful responsibility, supported to grow, and surrounded by people who share ideas and raise the bar together. Our Beyond Brilliant
values— Beyond the Status Quo
, Beyond Excellence
, Brilliant Together
, and Brilliant Experiences
—guide how we innovate, collaborate, deliver, and put people at the centre.

Offers within this range are determined based on relevant experience, skills, and qualifications, as well as internal equity considerations. This job posting is for an existing vacancy.

Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer, the Director of Finance & CFO serves as the District's Financial Officer and provides strategic leadership for financial stewardship, long-term sustainability, governance, and risk management. Financial Strategy & Governance

Cogir Senior Living manages retirement residences across the country. We offer a range of senior living options including independent living, assisted living and memory care.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Housing & Infrastructure
jobs.description:
The Inuvialuit Regional Corporation (IRC) is a uniquely positioned Indigenous organization dedicated to enhancing the economic, social, and cultural well-being of Inuvialuit beneficiaries through the implementation of the historic Inuvialuit Final Agreement (IFA). Established in 1984 and headquartered in Inuvik, Northwest Territories, IRC represents the collective interests of six Inuvialuit communities, including 35,000 square miles of Inuvialuit-owned lands. Today, IRC is a significant and multifaceted organization with more than 180 employees, $1.9 billion in assets, and a broad mandate spanning land stewardship, investment, economic development, health, education, culture, and community development. Through its diverse operations, subsidiaries, programs, and partnerships, IRC plays a central role in advancing Inuvialuit participation in the northern economy while supporting the long-term prosperity, self-determination, and well-being of Inuvialuit communities.

Reporting directly to the Chair and Chief Executive Officer, the Managing Director, Housing & Infrastructure will lead IRC’s capacity to plan and deliver housing, community facilities, and major infrastructure across the Inuvialuit Settlement Region. This is represented by four key functions: Programme Planning and Controls, Housing Delivery, Owner’s Engineering and Assurance, and Infrastructure Delivery. Housing represents the most immediate and substantial priority, with more than 150 units currently forecast to 2030, and a further assessed need of more than 1,000 units by 2040. Beyond delivering individual projects, the Managing Director will help establish the longer-term master planning, standardized approaches, project controls, procurement strategies, and supply-chain solutions needed to accelerate housing and infrastructure development across IRC’s communities. They will also act as owner’s representative for several infrastructure projects related to NORAD’s Forward Operating Location in Inuvik working closely with the Canadian Department of National Defense. And they will plan and deliver additional infrastructure in the region to support the projected population growth and increased activity.

The role will require breadth as much as scale. IRC’s growing capital portfolio spans housing, community, energy, transportation, logistics, commercial, and other major infrastructure. Each element of this portfolio is shaped by the realities of remote northern delivery, short construction seasons, constrained logistics, and limited resupply windows. As the ideal candidate, you bring extensive experience leading complex, multidisciplinary capital programs across the full project lifecycle and, ideally, demonstrated experience delivering in the North or Arctic. Exceptional leaders from similarly remote, logistically constrained, or uniquely complex environments will also be relevant. Above all, the Managing Director will hold the owner’s seat, and be responsible for setting requirements, challenging designers and contractors, managing cost and schedule, and ensuring projects are delivered safely, practically, and to IRC’s expectations.

This is an opportunity to build an enduring infrastructure capability within IRC and leave a lasting positive impact across the entire region and the nation. The Managing Director will establish and lead each of the four key functions, building a permanent internal team while effectively directing seconded personnel and external delivery partners. For a practical, purpose-driven leader attracted to complex delivery and northern development, the opportunity combines immediate execution with the chance to create the systems, capability, and Inuvialuit capacity required to support IRC’s communities and ambitions for decades to come.

To explore this opportunity further, please click ‘apply’.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Client Families
jobs.description:
About Us

Mayfair is a private family office. We design, build and run the office that sits around a principal’s wealth and their life, so the people who created that wealth don’t have to run it themselves.

The people who join now will shape what Mayfair becomes, from how we bring on new principals to how we work together. Your work will show up in the company as much as in the principals you serve.

The Role

You’ll run the office for each principal you serve. You’ll be their single point of contact and direct the work across our five verticals. You’ll sit beside the principal, not three layers below them, and see the whole picture rather than one slice of it. Your judgment shapes real outcomes for the people we serve. You’ll work with a small number of principals. How many depends on the level of service each one has chosen. You become the person they call first. When something needs a decision, you bring it to them with the work done and the options framed. The decisions stay with them.

You won’t carry the work alone. Our own people run the five verticals behind you, and AI handles much of the research, reporting, and document prep underneath. That leaves your time for the principal and the judgment calls.

You don’t need to be an expert in all matters. You need to know when a question calls for a specialist, bring in the right people, and make sure the principal has what they need to decide. Knowing who to call matters more than knowing every answer.

What You'll Do

• Become the principal’s right hand, and build the relationship over years, not quarters.
• Run the reporting and meeting cadence so the principal knows what’s coming before it arrives.
• Keep the decision log. When something needs a decision, bring it with the work done and the options framed.
• Have the difficult conversations when they come up, whether that’s telling a principal a plan won’t work, holding an advisor to a missed deadline, or helping family members work through a disagreement.
• Direct our Asset Administration & Reporting, Banking & Treasury, Financial Operations, Wealth Oversight and Tax & Structures teams so the work gets done well and on time. In a given month that might mean signing off the bill pay schedule, approving a capital call, reviewing the monthly close and cash forecast, or planning the tax work ahead of a business sale.
• Oversee the life side of the office: property managers, household staff, aviation, travel, IT and security.
• Put governance and controls in place, from approval limits to how payments are authorized, and keep them working.
• Hold the principal’s lawyers, accountants, bankers and investment managers accountable to one plan and one set of facts.
• Spot early when a situation needs a specialist. You don’t need to be the expert, but you need to know when one is needed. If a principal is heading toward a sale, the tax and legal team should be in place months before the deal, not the week it closes.
• Lead triage for new principals: map every advisor, account, entity and asset, learn the principal’s values, and set up how they want approvals to work.
• Help shape how Mayfair onboards, reports and runs reviews as the company grows.

What We're Looking For

• Five or more years at manager or senior manager level in a Big Four private client group, or a comparable role in private banking, wealth advisory or a multi-family office, including leading complex, multi-advisor projects for ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families.
• Strong emotional intelligence. You read people well and earn trust quickly. You notice what a principal isn’t saying, stay steady when a conversation gets difficult, and can tell them something they don’t want to hear. This matters more than anything else on this list.
• Ease with significant wealth. You’re comfortable with founders, executives and multi-generational families, and you hold your own with them and with their lawyer, accountant and banker in the same room.
• A generalist’s curiosity. One week it’s a pre-sale reorganization, the next it’s an aircraft purchase, a new trust or a renovation. You don’t need to be the expert in each. What matters is learning enough to run it and knowing when to bring in someone who is.
• Clear, simple communication. You can take something complex and make it simple. A principal should be able to read your summary in five minutes and know the options, the trade-offs and what needs deciding.
• A CPA, TEP, CFA or equivalent professional designation.
• Flexibility to work across North American time zones. Some travel is required, in Canada and the US.
• You live in Canada and are legally entitled to work in Canada.

Nice to Have

• Experience at an early startup, ideally one still defining its own operating model while building.
• Background in wealth tech, legal tech, or fintech.
• Working familiarity with family office concepts: trusts, entity structures, investment policy statements, manager oversight, and how those pieces interact.
• Experience working alongside a small team without a large product organization or established tooling around you.
• A CPA In-Depth or Master of Taxation, Canada and US cross-border experience, or time in a family office.

Logistics

• Remote, based anywhere in Canada. Full-time and permanent.
• Base salary range: $165,000 to $185,000 CAD per year. Where you land in the range reflects your experience.
• Standard business hours, with flexibility across North American time zones.
• Some travel is required, in Canada and the US.

How We Hire

Five values guide how we work:
Do What Is Right.
Be In The Arena.
Earn The Right.
All In. One Team.
Fear Nothing. Solve Everything.
They are the first filter for anyone who joins us, ahead of the interview and ahead of skills.

Because this role approves client payments and other financial transactions, the process includes a background check, including a credit check, with your written consent.

We give everyone we interview an answer.

How to Apply

Apply through LinkedIn with your resume. We highly recommend a cover letter. Make it the first page of the same PDF you upload as your resume.

In the first line of your cover letter, tell us your favourite restaurant, or a place you would take a visitor, in the city where you live.

Mayfair welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, tell us and we’ll work with you.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

About Us

As Canada’s # 1 retailer of cell phones, The Wireless Kiosk @ Costco operates in every Canadian warehouse coast-coast. Our highly trained kiosk Advisors provide unbiased solutions  to some of the most engaged, affluent and loyal consumers in the country. So, it stands to reason that if we are serving the best of the best clientele, we only hire the best of the best leaders to run our business.

Director Role

Lead leaders. Shape culture. Drive transformation. Build the future!!

We view performance results as an OUTPUT.

OUTPUTS are delivered through actions, behaviors and activity – which we call INPUTS

Too often, we see sales associates and sales managers chasing outputs, which are sometimes known as KPI’s and pushing employees into “closing” customers. We have also seen that this “push” promotes solutions that do not fit what the customer actually needs. This short-term thinking approach we view as unsustainable and does not promote medium to long term growth

Our view is based upon focusing on INPUTS and we are strong believers that if you do the right thing, with the right people, in the right way, at the right time – you will invariably get the right result – the OUTPUT. We also strongly believe that OUTPUTS driven by proper INPUTS, provide the foundation for sustainable on-going growth.

The Director of Retail Operations is a leadership role which requires the right candidate to be able to operate both strategically and tactically (based upon the needs of our business) and is responsible for executing our operational go to market strategy.

Our team across the country is 600+ strong and they are the backbone of our operations. You will be responsible for leading our Western Canadian employees and growing our business through INFLUENCE, building CONSTITUENCY and showing your IMPACT through superior EXECUTION.

The key to winning at retail is the quality of our front-line people. Finding, recruiting, training and successfully onboarding is the foundation of any retailer’s success. This requires us to have hiring clarity on the profile of individual that we are looking for as well as determining who is a suitable candidate and who is not. We have found that this is key to developing and properly casting new hires into roles that match their strengths.

You will report into the Senior Director of Operation and be responsible for leading our business in 40+ locations and will be supporting 3 District Managers. This role requires you to be accountable for creating a high-performance culture where behaviors, execution and results are aligned. You will support our over-arching strategy and with the help of your leadership team, execute the tactical plan developed. You will drive organizational effectiveness (and change, where required) and ensures the creation of sustainable success by developing a strong leadership bench, identifying future talent, and guiding your teams through cyclical periods of growth, transformation, and change.

The ideal candidate must be influential and has impact when they communicate and are able to build constituency with other stakeholders and who can balance strategy with high levels of execution. The ideal candidate will also be able to challenge the status quo, can make difficult decisions, and inspire others to embrace change, while remaining focused and true to the execution of our strategy and operational plan.

What You Will Shine At

Leading and developing a team of District Managers and field leaders across a large and complex geographic region.
Driving organizational performance through strategic execution, accountability, and operational excellence.
Building leadership capability at all levels through coaching, mentorship, and succession planning.
Identifying opportunities to improve productivity, effectiveness, and business outcomes across the region.
Creating a culture of high performance, continuous improvement & accountability
Developing and executing talent strategies that attract, retain, and advance top performers.
Challenging leaders to think differently, improve execution, and raise performance standards.
Strengthening partnerships with Costco leadership through credibility, trust, and a shared commitment to delivering a world-class member experience.

Who You Are

You have 10+ years of progressive leadership experience leading large, multi-site teams through other leaders.
You have a proven track record of improving business performance through people, process, and execution.
You are an exceptional “change leader” who can create alignment, navigate ambiguity, and help teams embrace new ways of working.
You have successfully led organizational transformations, restructures, large-scale business initiatives, or performance turnarounds.
You are skilled at developing District Managers, senior leaders, and high-potential talent.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Few organizations have the reach, relationships and opportunity to shape community well-being across British Columbia quite like United Way British Columbia ("UWBC"). As one of the province's most recognized and influential charitable organizations, UWBC brings together people, resources, expertise and partners to tackle ever-evolving and pressing social challenges. Built on a proud legacy of community leadership, UWBC is unique in its ability to offer both deep local expertise and the reach and influence of a province-wide organization.

Not the United Way you may think you know.

Founded on a federated fundraising/grantor model and largely based on workplace campaigns, the organization has very deliberately moved toward partnered program delivery, community mobilization and solutions designed around demonstrated gaps. The impact of this shift can be seen in every corner of the province. An historic amalgamation of regional United Way organizations, as well as a merger with BC211, has enhanced the strategic capability of the organization. Today, UWBC is what most social impact organizations can only aspire to be: a high profile social impact organization with local presence; provincial scale; specialist expertise; strong government relationships at all levels, and enviable capacity to innovate.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”) will lead UWBC into an exciting new chapter. Following the tenure of a long-serving leader, the next CEO joins at an exciting juncture. With an opportunity to shape the development of the next strategic plan, and supported by a committed Board and team, this leader will play an important role in advancing United Way BC’s mission and strengthening its high-profile impact across the province. The Board is looking to the next CEO to sharpen the organization’s strategic focus, strengthen financial sustainability and funding opportunities and establish greater clarity around where UWBC can deliver the greatest impact.

As the next CEO, you are a proven, forward-thinking and values-driven leader who has demonstrated an ability to lead an organization through ongoing change. Collaborative and inspiring, you have a track record of translating strategy into results, building capacity at an enterprise level and fostering partnerships that drive organizational success. Combining financial and operational acumen with exceptional leadership, relationship-building skills and political awareness, you bring the credibility, courage and commitment to advance UWBC's mission and strengthen its impact at a time when communities across British Columbia are facing increasingly complex social challenges. The power of collective action has never been more important. UWBC stands at the forefront of this work, bringing together communities, partners and resources to create meaningful and lasting impact.

The compensation for this role is in the range of $300,000 - $330,000, plus an attractive benefits package, including participation in the Municipal Pension Plan.

UWBC’s headquarters are in Burnaby, BC. This role provides for the opportunity to travel across British Columbia and get to know this great province.

Job Description

The Senior Director, ISV Business Development is the global craft leader for Sage’s ISV ecosystem. You will act as the single accountable owner for turning solution strategy into ecosystem-led, commercially-governed growth. Operating as the head of the ISV craft, the role holds unified accountability for solution-strategy alignment, commercial contracting, go-to-market (GTM) success support, executive relationship management, and partner performance across every business unit, franchise and region.

This role sits at the intersection of Product Management, Product Marketing, Growth, Enablement, Performance Marketing, Trading, Legal, Finance and Regional Revenue teams. It exists to ensure that the BUILD / Partner / Buy decision is made deliberately and consistently, that the resulting commercial relationships are contracted on scalable terms, and that partners are launched, supported and held to measurable annual targets – so that ecosystem investment is always tied directly to customer outcomes and revenue.

This is a Hybrid position based in-office 3 days per week.

Key Responsibilities

Solution Strategy Alignment (BUILD / Partner / Buy)

Own the partner voice in solution strategy – partner with Product Management and Product Marketing to bring clarity to the BUILD, Partner or Buy decision for each capability gap, ensuring the right capability reaches customers through the right commercial model.
Steward the Solution Maps – maintain the partner component of Sage’s global solution maps, translating identified capability gaps into a prioritized ecosystem investment and recruitment plan.
Guard the BUILD boundary – ensure that where Sage chooses to build, ISV extensibility, AI-gateway readiness and self-funding business-development principles are designed in, so partner strategy strengthens rather than duplicates the core roadmap.
Governance – run the quarterly connect / review cadence that keeps Product, Growth, Marketing, Enablement, Sales and Commercial Partner teams aligned to a single, consistent solution strategy across geographies.

Commercial Contracting

Chief commercial contracting authority for ISV – lead negotiation of global reseller, referral, OEM, white-label, marketplace, co-sell and strategic alliance agreements.
Scalable frameworks – develop and institutionalize standard commercial frameworks, pricing structures, revenue-share and API-monetization models, and policy standards that apply consistently across all Sage products and regions.
Cross-functional integrity – partner closely with Legal, Finance, Product and Operations to ensure commercial consistency, sound unit economics and end-to-end alignment to signed commitments.

GTM Success Support

Launch readiness – drive the five-phase activation lifecycle (approval and scope, commercial and systems readiness, product and technical readiness, GTM enablement and launch, post-GA performance management) so every partnership is commercially viable, technically sound and operationally ready before launch.
Enablement and handoff – ensure clean handoff to Commercial Operations, Enablement and field sellers (direct and channel), with playbooks, positioning and rules of engagement that let sellers support and position ISV solutions independently.
Field execution support – work with regional revenue and growth teams so strategic partners receive the visibility, overlay capacity and commercial guidance needed to convert strategy into pipeline and attach.

Relationship Management

Executive sponsorship – maintain trusted executive-level relationships and governance for Sage’s most strategic ISV partnerships, representing Sage as a senior partner in the market.
Joint business planning – develop and execute joint business plans, and lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and executive steering committees with top ISV partners.
Final escalation point – act as the ultimate escalation owner for strategic partner matters, resolving complex commercial, product, legal and GTM issues and protecting long-term mutual growth.

Partner Performance – Annual Target Setting & Performance Reporting

Annual target setting – work with partners and regional revenue leaders to set annual ISV targets, ensuring ISV revenue is budgeted as an explicit subset of franchise revenue with assigned sales targets rather than left as unowned aspiration.
Performance reporting – own the ISV scorecard and regular reporting to leadership – tracking ISV-sourced and ISV-influenced ARR, net revenue and margin contribution, attach rate, retention/expansion, activation and churn.

Course correction – run monthly and quarterly performance reviews to track partners against target, and recommend investment, expansion or corrective action to keep the portfolio performing.

Approximately 15+ years of relevant industry experience, particularly in ISV business development.
Proven experience leading people, beyond individual contributor success.
Leadership Approach: A “first among equals” leadership style, guiding four largely self-directed, director-level professionals.
Ability to act as a mentor, sounding board, and advisor rather than relying on detailed direction or hands-on management.
Leverages experience to provide guidance, anticipate challenges, and help the team navigate risks.
