Job Information

Job Title: Director Emerging Resources.

Job Requisition ID: 89476

Ministry: Energy and Minerals

Location: Edmonton or Calgary

Full or Part-Time: Full-time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Permanent

Scope: Open Competition

Closing Date: November 29, 2026

Classification: Senior Manager, Zone 2

Salary: $5,139.30 - $6,526.16 bi-weekly ($134,135 - $170,332/year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

The Ministry of Energy and Minerals is responsible for sustaining the interests of Albertans through the stewardship and responsible development of energy and mineral resource systems.

Please review Energy and Minerals to learn more and what it has to offer.

The Strategy and Market Access (SAMA) Division is responsible for developing Alberta's strategic direction to deliver on energy mandates including natural gas infrastructure development, market access, energy market diversification, strategic foresight, economic analysis, and stakeholder engagement.

The Energy Futures Branch leads the development and implementation of strategies related to natural gas infrastructure, value-add initiatives, export opportunities including liquefied natural gas (LNG) and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), critical minerals, emerging resources, and pipeline regulatory processes

The Unit of Emerging Resources is responsible for strategy development and implementation of Alberta’s critical minerals and geo-thermal resources.

Role Responsibilities

Are you a strategic thinker and collaborative leader? Energy Futures is looking for a Director, Emerging Resources to provide strategic leadership and advance Alberta’s critical minerals, geothermal energy, and other emerging resource opportunities.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Energy Futures, this position provides strategic leadership for the Department’s mandated initiatives related to critical minerals, geothermal and other emerging opportunities. The position leads professional teams responsible for strategy and legislative development, complex projects, and work across government and with external partners to advance complex policy, investment, regulatory, and market priorities.

In This Role, You Will

Provide strategic advice, analysis and recommendations, for policies, programs, and initiatives related to critical minerals, geothermal energy, and other emerging resources.
Lead strategy planning, legislative and regulatory development, implementation planning and evaluation for Alberta’s Critical Minerals Strategy and Action Plan and other emerging resource development initiatives.
Direct the preparation of decision documents, briefing notes, correspondence, cabinet and Treasury Board materials, key messages and other executive products.
Lead complex, cross-ministry and cross-jurisdictional initiatives including engagement with federal, provincial and territorial partnerships on critical minerals.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with federal counterparts and industry to advance Alberta’s interests and strategic outcomes on critical minerals and other emerging opportunities. Lead, coach, and develop managers and staff while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and results-oriented work environment.
Identify opportunities to strengthen Alberta’s competitiveness, attract investment, and support mineral exploration, development, processing, and value-added opportunities.
Direct complex policy, economic, technical, regulatory, and market analysis and provide evidence-based recommendations to senior and executive leadership.
Represent the department on intergovernmental committees, working groups, industry forums, and other strategic initiatives.
Lead unit operations, workforce planning, financial oversights, priority setting, staff development, issues management and coordination oversight and continuous improvement while managing competing priorities and emerging issues.

This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic and collaborative leader to influence Alberta’s energy and mineral future. Your leadership will help shape policies, strengthen partnerships, attract investment, and advance the responsible development of Alberta’s emerging resources.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Systems Thinking: You will consider the broader economic, regulatory, competitive, and market environment when developing strategies for critical minerals, geothermal energy, and emerging resources.
Build Collaborative Environments: You will build strategic relationships with industry, Indigenous organizations, regulators, other governments, and cross-ministry partners to advance emerging resource priorities.
Develop Self and Others: You will provide clear direction, coaching, and mentorship to managers and staff, empowering your team to deliver on complex priorities. This aligns with the APS emphasis on achieving results through others and setting clear expectations.
Creative Problem Solving: You will analyze complex policy, economic, regulatory, and market issues and develop practical, evidence-based options and recommendations for senior leadership.
Drive for Results: You will establish clear priorities and lead the delivery of high-profile strategic initiatives while balancing competing priorities and maintaining accountability for results.

jobs.title: Associate Director - Sponsor Coverage
jobs.description:
At ATB, we exist to make it possible for our clients, team members and communities. Our purpose is more than aspirational. It's a real commitment we live every day through our values (what we call the ATB ID).

About

Life at ATB is about more than work. In fact, we’re consistently recognized as one of Canada's top employers thanks to our high-care, high-performance culture, upheld by the three commitments we make to our team members:

Impact in action:
No matter where you are in the organization, you're empowered to make an impact in the lives of our clients and communities.

Thrive together:
We want you—the unique, authentic you—to feel safe and celebrated at work. We're on a continuous journey to build the most flexible and inclusive programs.

Ready for tomorrow:
We want to enable your success through interesting and challenging work, performance enablement, and learning and development.

Leadership is in our DNA at ATB, reflecting our commitment to developing world-class leaders who can truly thrive. Our Leader DNA model sets the standard for how we lead people, drive business performance, and shape a dynamic future. This is the place for purpose-driven individuals ready to deliver impactful leadership every day.

About The Team

The ATB Sponsor Coverage team is a specialized lending and coverage group focused on sponsors and the mid-market businesses they own. The team provides cash-flow-based senior lending and full capital solutions to support sponsor-led acquisitions, leveraged buyouts, recapitalizations, refinancings, growth capital and follow-on acquisitions - and then stays with those portfolio companies through the life of the investment.

Working through ATB's integrated client service model, the team partners closely with ATB Cormark Capital Markets, Investment Banking, Loan Syndications, and Financial Markets, as well as with Credit, Risk and our industry coverage teams, to deliver debt, equity, interest rate, foreign exchange and other capital solutions through one deal team.

About The Role

As ATB's next Associate Director - Sponsor Coverage, you are someone who loves solving problems and connecting with people, is client obsessed, and leverages their financial skills to find ways to create a meaningful impact on our clients. You will help deliver deep coverage of financial sponsor relationships and ensure the overall quality and credit risk of a portfolio of sponsor-backed borrowers.

You are a point of contact for clients and sponsors on senior debt and credit matters via analysis, structuring, and collaborating across multiple teams to meet client needs and ensure flawless execution. Working closely with the Senior Director, Sponsor Coverage, you will anticipate and respond to sponsor and portfolio company needs, assist with structuring competitive financing packages, and protect the quality of the portfolio at the same time.

Accountabilities

Sponsor coverage

Build and deepen relationships with sponsors, their portfolio companies, and intermediary and lender contacts, maintaining a current view of the sponsor market and of each sponsor's investment strategy, track record and active portfolio.
Assist in identifying and assessing new financing opportunities, origination and pitch activity, prepare and present financing proposals — including structure, terms and conditions, security, covenants and pricing - to sponsors and prospective clients.
Attend meetings with sponsor and portfolio company management to assess financing needs, and develop good relationships with internal stakeholders, external clients and general industry contacts.
Identify opportunities for ancillary and cross-sell business and refer or respond to them with partners in ATB Cormark Capital Markets, Investment Banking, Loan Syndications, Financial Markets and other areas of ATB.
Participate in Sales Team meetings, sharing successes, best practices, market intelligence and other information.

Transaction execution

On Each Transaction You Will Support The Senior Sales Director From First Assessment Through To Disbursement, Operating With Autonomy And Accountability, Including

Completing comprehensive due diligence on new opportunities — business, industry, financial, commercial, legal and accounting — identifying and substantiating key risks and mitigants, and completing sponsor due diligence, including investment track record, returns and alignment with capital providers.
Structuring and participating in the creation of term sheets and deal structures that solve the sponsor's and the portfolio company's current and future needs, and recommending alternative terms, conditions and covenants that make a proposal bankable within sound lending practice.
Preparation and negotiation of legal documentation including term sheets, commitment and fee letters, credit agreements and security documents in partnership with legal counsel.
Ensuring prompt follow-up for acceptance of authorizations, and reacting swiftly to problems, amendments and extensions, reporting to the Sales Director and senior management where necessary.
Overseeing disbursement of loans within authorized lending limits once credit approval, required documentation, collateral and security are in place, and coordinating closing activities with sponsors, borrowers, syndicate lenders and internal partners.
On amendment, extension and syndication transactions, support the Sales Director as a point of contact for the client and lenders, as well as managing transaction timelines end to end.

Accountabilities

Credit analysis and portfolio management

Manage a portfolio focused on the senior debt relationship with sponsor-backed clients, promoting loan growth through outstanding credit awareness and identifying opportunities to further the profitability of the portfolio.
Prepare credit assessments through completion of applications for credit, which includes analyzing financial statements and information to assess risk and determine which ATB services meet the client's needs; financial modelling and sensitivity analysis of projections; capital structure analysis with recommendations on alternate capital structures; understanding credit ratings and return assessments, with recommendations on any impact to profitability and the cost and availability of capital; and valuation and security analysis with relevant recommendations.
Develop and maintain comprehensive, company-specific financial models to evaluate cash-flow and leveraged lending scenarios, with a focus on understanding cash flows, debt capacity, leverage and debt service under base and downside cases.
Monitor the portfolio on an ongoing basis to ensure it is managed against ATB's targets: track financial covenants, borrowing conditions and internal reporting requirements, complete monitoring and control processes in a timely manner, and identify negative trends early so corrective action can be taken.
Stay abreast of current market conditions, leveraged lending trends and comparable transactions, and provide market feedback on structures and pricing to deal teams, credit officers and other internal parties.

Risk management

Demonstrate ownership and oversight with sound credit practices to mitigate and control the risks related to the portfolio, ensuring all activities are conducted in compliance with governing regulations, internal policies and procedures.
Ensure credit decisions and recommendations are in accordance with sound credit granting principles and ATB's lending policy and procedures, and maintain ATB's risk appetite, conditions of credit and documentation.
Build and maintain a strong working relationship with ATB's Credit and Risk groups, engaging early on structures, leverage and exceptions.
Act as a point of contact for internal and external audit activities.

Subject matter expertise

Use industry, sponsor and analytical expertise to provide recommendations and insight into client solutions, and to support preparation for client interactions.
Develop recognized subject matter expertise in sponsor-backed and leveraged lending, syndications, and in the industries represented in the portfolio.
Represent ATB by attending and supporting networking and community events focused on developing connections with clients and the industry.

Team collaboration and coaching

Motivate team members and internal partners to ensure flawless execution for our clients, and create strong relationships with clients.
Provide guidance, coaching and counsel to other Associate Directors and Associates and support Team Members assigned to the portfolio, so that client service expectations and credit quality are maintained, and share best practices and transaction experience with peers across ATB Business.
Develop a strong knowledge of ATB products and services available to our clients, and an intimate knowledge of the internal partner groups and processes required to align the institution to serve clients.

Skills, Experience & Requirements

Leading transactions end to end, exercising sound credit judgement independently, and representing ATB credibly with sponsors, borrowers, and lenders.
5-7+ years of experience with a financial institution in progressively more complex roles focused on corporate or commercial lending, corporate finance, investment banking or sponsor coverage.
Proven track record in specialized senior lending, including acquisition financing, leveraged lending and loan syndication, with a preference for sponsor finance or leveraged buyout experience.
An undergraduate degree in business, commerce, economics, finance or a related quantitative field. A Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) or CPA designation, or graduate-level education such as an MBA, would be an asset.
Demonstrated leadership in a financial capacity with a strong working knowledge of corporate finance credit products and services, complex loan documentation, and capital structure alternatives, and the standing to lead negotiations with sponsors, borrowers and syndicate lenders.
Exceptional analytical capability and financial acumen, including strong financial modelling and accounting skills and proven ability to build financial analysis for mid- to large-sized organizations and complex business issues.
Exceptional credit, analytical and problem-solving skills, with advanced initiative to find and execute innovative solutions within ATB's risk appetite.
Strong communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to present complex issues effectively at all levels, influence others, and build relationships with external clients, sponsors and internal teammates.
Demonstrated collaborative skills working with senior management and specialists, with the ability to influence and coordinate a team, and to engage in active dialogue with internal and external stakeholders, including clients, legal counsel and credit partners.
Excellent priority and organizational management, with the capability to manage multiple transactions, initiatives and daily activity to meet client needs and tight transaction deadlines, with close attention to detail.
Proven ability to build impactful relationships across all levels of the organization, and a demonstrated pursuit of excellence inside or outside work, with the ability to adapt to diverse situations.
Working knowledge of Google Workspace products, Microsoft Office products, including Excel, PowerPoint and Word and Ai platforms to increase productivity is required.

Don’t meet all the requirements on the list?

A resume only goes so far in expressing who you are and the unique perspectives you bring. If you believe your skills and experience align with the role—but you might not check all the boxes—we want to hear from you. We encourage candidates from all work backgrounds, equity-seeking communities and experience levels to apply. If you’re seeking a career where your drive, perspective and growth are celebrated, we want to hear from you.

The Corporate Finance team within Canadian Commercial Banking, is part of BMO Financial group and covers both public and large private corporate clients operating in diversified industries. This role requires a combination of advanced financial analysis, strong credit analysis and relationship management abilities. Associate Directors contribute to client decisioning, credit structuring, and portfolio oversight, while also supporting new business development and delivering a superior client experience. Work is performed in close partnership with Managing Director and/or Director. The deal team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. Analyzes credit information to support lending decisions and processes for new and existing Commercial banking loans and credit solutions in an assigned portfolio of clients. Makes credit decisions and recommendations in compliance with bank policies and procedures while maintaining an exceptional client service environment.

Negotiates loan structures and terms and conditions that align client requirements with the bank risk appetite and policies.
Assesses client repayment capacity by utilizing financial models and analytical tools to recommend appropriate loan structures and collateral requirements.

Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations.

Bachelor’s degree required; Business Administration, Finance and Accounting preferred. Any other related discipline or commensurate work experience considered.

Problem Solving

Customer Service

Regulatory Compliance
Portfolio Management

please submit your cover letter and current resume by email to Chris Sawyer, Senior Consultant, at chris.sawyer@lhhknightsbridge.com .

THE ORGANIZATION

Unity Health Toronto is one of Canada’s largest Catholic healthcare networks serving patients, residents and clients across the full spectrum of care, spanning primary care, secondary community care, tertiary and quaternary care services to post-acute through rehabilitation, palliative care and long-term care, while investing in world-class research and education.

Research is a cornerstone of Unity Health Toronto’s mission, bringing together world-class scientists, clinician-researchers, trainees, and research staff to advance discoveries that improve patient care and strengthen health systems. With internationally recognized strengths across clinical, scientific, and population health research, Unity Health is committed to translating innovative research into meaningful impact for patients, communities, and the broader healthcare system.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Clinical trials are a key part of Unity Health Toronto's Exceptional Care Without Exception strategic plan, advancing research excellence across the network while providing patients with access to innovative therapeutics that may not otherwise be available. SPHERE CRO , one of Canada's leading academically-affiliated Contract Research Organizations (CRO), complements this work by delivering end-to-end clinical research services to academic, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and industry partners, including site management, project management, data management and technologies, regulatory affairs, biostatistics, and patient engagement.

A newly-created role reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, Research, and overseeing a team of approximately 50 people, the Senior Director will lead the execution of Unity’s clinical trials strategy, including the build of the Central Clinical Trials Unit, the adoption of key technologies such as the enterprise deployment of the clinical trials management system, and initiatives that position Unity’s sites as a global leader in clinical trials performance. The Senior Director will also lead the Industry Preferred Partnership Model, further fostering relationships with existing global pharmaceutical partners while pursuing new partnerships aligned with Unity’s clinical trials strategy. new_jobs.description:
The Inuvialuit Regional Corporation (IRC) is a uniquely positioned Indigenous organization dedicated to enhancing the economic, social, and cultural well-being of Inuvialuit beneficiaries through the implementation of the historic Inuvialuit Final Agreement (IFA). Established in 1984 and headquartered in Inuvik, Northwest Territories, IRC represents the collective interests of six Inuvialuit communities, including 35,000 square miles of Inuvialuit-owned lands. Today, IRC is a significant and multifaceted organization with more than 180 employees, $1.9 billion in assets, and a broad mandate spanning land stewardship, investment, economic development, health, education, culture, and community development. Through its diverse operations, subsidiaries, programs, and partnerships, IRC plays a central role in advancing Inuvialuit participation in the northern economy while supporting the long-term prosperity, self-determination, and well-being of Inuvialuit communities.

Reporting directly to the Chair and Chief Executive Officer, the Managing Director, Housing & Infrastructure will lead IRC’s capacity to plan and deliver housing, community facilities, and major infrastructure across the Inuvialuit Settlement Region. This is represented by four key functions: Programme Planning and Controls, Housing Delivery, Owner’s Engineering and Assurance, and Infrastructure Delivery. Housing represents the most immediate and substantial priority, with more than 150 units currently forecast to 2030, and a further assessed need of more than 1,000 units by 2040. Beyond delivering individual projects, the Managing Director will help establish the longer-term master planning, standardized approaches, project controls, procurement strategies, and supply-chain solutions needed to accelerate housing and infrastructure development across IRC’s communities. They will also act as owner’s representative for several infrastructure projects related to NORAD’s Forward Operating Location in Inuvik working closely with the Canadian Department of National Defense. And they will plan and deliver additional infrastructure in the region to support the projected population growth and increased activity.

The role will require breadth as much as scale. IRC’s growing capital portfolio spans housing, community, energy, transportation, logistics, commercial, and other major infrastructure. Each element of this portfolio is shaped by the realities of remote northern delivery, short construction seasons, constrained logistics, and limited resupply windows. As the ideal candidate, you bring extensive experience leading complex, multidisciplinary capital programs across the full project lifecycle and, ideally, demonstrated experience delivering in the North or Arctic. Exceptional leaders from similarly remote, logistically constrained, or uniquely complex environments will also be relevant. Above all, the Managing Director will hold the owner’s seat, and be responsible for setting requirements, challenging designers and contractors, managing cost and schedule, and ensuring projects are delivered safely, practically, and to IRC’s expectations.

This is an opportunity to build an enduring infrastructure capability within IRC and leave a lasting positive impact across the entire region and the nation. The Managing Director will establish and lead each of the four key functions, building a permanent internal team while effectively directing seconded personnel and external delivery partners. For a practical, purpose-driven leader attracted to complex delivery and northern development, the opportunity combines immediate execution with the chance to create the systems, capability, and Inuvialuit capacity required to support IRC’s communities and ambitions for decades to come.

Founded on a federated fundraising/grantor model and largely based on workplace campaigns, the organization has very deliberately moved toward partnered program delivery, community mobilization and solutions designed around demonstrated gaps. Collaborative and inspiring, you have a track record of translating strategy into results, building capacity at an enterprise level and fostering partnerships that drive organizational success. Combining financial and operational acumen with exceptional leadership, relationship-building skills and political awareness, you bring the credibility, courage and commitment to advance UWBC's mission and strengthen its impact at a time when communities across British Columbia are facing increasingly complex social challenges. All our investments stem from a common thesis, that travel advisors add real value to a trip. Travel advisors when equipped with technology and 24/7 support are irreplaceable. Equally important is our philanthropy. Range Foundation channels 10% of group profits to social impact. From exploration grants, improved access to education, new discoveries on sea and land, cultural infrastructure, and helping our global neighbors in times of need — we are investing to build a better future.

About The Role

This is a hands-on senior finance leadership role for someone who operates at the intersection of strategy, analytics, and execution. You’re as comfortable building a complex multi-entity model from scratch as you are presenting the story behind the numbers to the executive team.

As Director, FP&A, you will own the analytical engine that supports decision-making across Range Group’s portfolio of travel brands — leading enterprise planning and forecasting, managing a small team, and working directly with senior leadership to evaluate opportunities, navigate risks, and drive performance.

What You’ll Do

Financial Modelling & Planning

Build, maintain, and continuously improve financial models covering consolidated Group performance, brand-level P&Ls, cash flow forecasting, and scenario analysis.
Own the Group-level cash flow tracker and EBITDA bridging model, ensuring accuracy and timeliness week over week.
Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes across the organization.
Support ad hoc financial analysis — acquisition modelling, business case development, and covenant compliance.
Drive continuous improvement in financial planning frameworks, forecasting methodologies, and analytical tools.

Performance Management & Executive Insights

Own enterprise-wide performance reporting — financial reviews, KPI dashboards, executive scorecards, and variance commentary.
Lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with senior leadership.
Translate financial results into clear, decision-ready insights that prompt action.
Identify and proactively flag emerging risks, opportunities, and performance trends across the portfolio.

Strategic Business Partnership

Partner with executive and business leaders to align financial plans with strategic priorities and growth objectives.
Evaluate investments, business initiatives, and strategic opportunities through modelling and scenario analysis.
Provide financial leadership on strategic initiatives, business cases, and investment decisions.
Support executive and Board reporting requirements.

Treasury & Foreign Exchange Management

Own foreign exchange exposure tracking, reporting, and scenario analysis across the Group's multi-currency operations.
Partner with treasury, banking partners, and external advisors to evaluate foreign exchange risks and mitigation strategies.
Assess the financial impact of currency fluctuations on forecasts, budgets, cash flow, and business performance.
Develop recommendations and decision-support materials for leadership regarding FX risk management and capital planning.
Monitor market trends and currency movements, proactively identifying risks and opportunities that may impact business performance.

Team Leadership & Capability Building

Lead a small finance team — including a Finance Manager and intern — as a player-coach: owning models and analysis end-to-end while delegating and developing where appropriate.
Foster a high-performance, analytically rigorous culture within the team.
Support ERP and reporting tool improvements from a finance data and output perspective.
Champion the evolution of finance from a reporting function to a true strategic business partner.

What You’ll Bring

8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, Strategic Finance, or Finance Business Partnering — with a track record of owning complex models in a multi-entity environment.
Advanced Excel skills — non-negotiable. You build models from scratch, structure them for auditability, and are fast and precise in the tool.
Strong accounting foundation: you understand how the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement connect inside a model.
Proven experience leading enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes.
Experience analyzing foreign exchange exposure, multi-currency financial impacts, and scenario modelling within a corporate FP&A, finance, or strategic finance environment.
Strong executive presence, comfortable presenting to senior leadership and capable of influencing and constructively challenging stakeholders.
Experience in multi-entity and multi-currency operating environments.
CPA designation strongly preferred; candidates without the designation will be considered where technical skills and experience are strong.
Background in travel, technology, hospitality, or another fast-paced, multi-brand environment is an asset.

Who You Are

You are a builder. You prefer to own models end-to-end and take pride in work that is structured, auditable, and built to last.
You are intellectually curious and detail-oriented, but able to zoom out and connect the numbers to a broader business narrative.
You operate well with ambiguity and can manage competing priorities without losing accuracy or composure.
You are a collaborative leader who still wants to be close to the work — energized by doing, not just directing.
You communicate with a low-ego, peer-level style — credible with senior stakeholders, collegial with the broader team, and proactive about surfacing issues.

Why Join Range Group

This is a rare opportunity to bridge corporate finance and executive strategy in a multi-brand travel and technology portfolio. You’ll have genuine influence — shaping how capital is allocated, how performance is communicated, and how the finance function evolves as the company grows.

The role carries real complexity: multi-entity consolidations, multi-currency exposure, and a direct reporting line to the Chief Finance Officer. You’ll lead a small team and have the space to build the frameworks and processes that become the foundation for the company’s next phase.

Hybrid Work Model

We’re based in Toronto and targeting three days in office per week, with flexibility built in.

We provide a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. Employees have the opportunity to participate in incentive programs and compensation tied to business and individual performance. The actual compensation may vary depending on local market conditions, geography and relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience, and education/training.

We are committed to providing employment accommodation in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. If you require accommodation due to a disability at any stage of our hiring process, please advise us when completing your application.

The Range Group may use artificial intelligence throughout the recruitment process to screen, assess or select applicants for this position. These tools assist our hiring team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans.

We thank all candidates for their interest however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

new_jobs.title: Payroll Operate Services - Director
new_jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

Payroll is a business-critical function, and organizations are looking for more efficient, technology-enabled ways to deliver it.

We’re looking for a senior payroll or employment tax professional who knows the market, sees where it’s going and wants to turn those insights into growth.

As a Director in EY’s Payroll Operate team, you’ll lead significant client relationships and help organizations transform how payroll is managed through EY’s managed payroll services. You’ll oversee complex payroll operations and new client transitions, bring together people, process and technology, and help build scalable solutions that improve the payroll experience.

This is an opportunity to combine payroll leadership, client delivery and commercial thinking while helping shape the growth of EY’s Payroll Operate business in Canada and contribute to the global business.

This posting does not relate to an existing vacancy. We are actively recruiting for this strategic hire to support the continued growth and development of our business.

Your Key Responsibilities

Lead managed payroll services for complex client organizations, with accountability for quality, controls and client experience.
Build strong relationships with senior payroll, HR and finance leaders and provide practical guidance on payroll operations.
Lead new client implementations and transitions, establishing effective processes, governance and service expectations.
Oversee end-to-end payroll delivery, including processing, reconciliations, reporting and payments.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and automate payroll through technology and better ways of working.
Shape and grow the business by identifying market opportunities and expanding our work with Canadian and multinational organizations.
Grow client relationships and contribute to new opportunities, proposals and payroll solution design.
Develop high-performing teams through coaching, collaboration and clear leadership.

Skills And Attributes For Success

Strong knowledge of Canadian payroll and the end-to-end payroll lifecycle.
Understanding of global payroll and the ability to collaborate with colleagues across regions and countries to support organizations with global operations.
Deep familiarity with enterprise payroll and HRIS systems (e.g., ADP, Workday, Dayforce), multi-jurisdictional tax laws, and advanced data analytics/Excel proficiency
Experience leading complex payroll operations, implementations or managed services.
Ability to build credibility and strong relationships with senior clients.
A continuous improvement mindset and interest in payroll technology, automation and transformation.
Strong operational judgment with the ability to manage risk and resolve complex delivery challenges.
Collaborative leadership style with a focus on developing people and teams.

Qualifications

Typically, 10+ years of progressive payroll experience, including significant leadership responsibility.
A bachelor’s degree in business, accounting, finance, human resources or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
Strong knowledge of Canadian payroll requirements, processes, controls and reporting.
Experience leading payroll teams, complex implementations, client relationships or significant payroll programs.

Ideally, you’ll also have,

A PLP, PCP, CPA or other relevant professional designation.
Experience in managed payroll, outsourced payroll or a shared services environment.
Experience transitioning payroll operations to a new delivery model or provider.
Exposure to payroll technology, automation, data analytics or transformation.
Experience contributing to proposals, solution design or new client opportunities.

What We Look For

We’re looking for an experienced payroll leader who knows how to deliver payroll reliably at scale while continually looking for ways to make it better. You combine strong operational judgment with a client mindset and are comfortable leading change, solving complex delivery challenges and building strong teams. You’re also excited by the opportunity to strengthen client relationships and help grow EY’s Payroll Operate business.

What We Offer

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. In addition, our Total Rewards package allows you to decide which benefits are right for you and which ones help you create a solid foundation for your future. Our Total Rewards package includes a discretionary bonus program, a comprehensive medical, prescription drug and dental coverage plan, a defined contribution pension plan, a great vacation policy plus firm paid days that allow you to enjoy longer long weekends throughout the year, statutory holidays and paid personal days (based on province of residence), and a range of exciting programs and benefits designed to support your physical, financial and social well-being. Plus, we offer:

Support and coaching from some of the most engaging colleagues in the industry
Learning opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that’s right for you

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To help create the best experience during the recruitment process, please describe any accommodations you may need.

Inclusiveness at EY

Inclusiveness is at the heart of who we are and how we work. We’re committed to fostering an environment where differences are valued, policies and practices are equitable, and our people feel a sense of belonging. We embrace diversity and are committed to combating systemic racism, advancing gender equity and women in leadership, advocating for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, promoting our neuroinclusion and accessibility initiatives, and are dedicated to amplifying the voices of Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis) nationally as we strive towards reconciliation. Our diverse experiences, abilities, backgrounds, and perspectives make our people unique and help guide us. Because when people feel free to be their authentic selves at work, they bring their best and are empowered to build a better working world.

Learn about our commitment to Inclusiveness at https://www.ey.com/en_ca/about-us/corporate-responsibility/equity

EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

Payroll is a business-critical function, and organizations are looking for more efficient, technology-enabled ways to deliver it.

We’re looking for a senior payroll or employment tax professional who knows the market, sees where it’s going and wants to turn those insights into growth.

As a Director in EY’s Payroll Operate team, you’ll lead significant client relationships and help organizations transform how payroll is managed through EY’s managed payroll services. You’ll oversee complex payroll operations and new client transitions, bring together people, process and technology, and help build scalable solutions that improve the payroll experience.

This is an opportunity to combine payroll leadership, client delivery and commercial thinking while helping shape the growth of EY’s Payroll Operate business in Canada and contribute to the global business.

This posting does not relate to an existing vacancy. We are actively recruiting for this strategic hire to support the continued growth and development of our business.

Your Key Responsibilities

Lead managed payroll services for complex client organizations, with accountability for quality, controls and client experience.
Build strong relationships with senior payroll, HR and finance leaders and provide practical guidance on payroll operations.
Lead new client implementations and transitions, establishing effective processes, governance and service expectations.
Oversee end-to-end payroll delivery, including processing, reconciliations, reporting and payments.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and automate payroll through technology and better ways of working.
Shape and grow the business by identifying market opportunities and expanding our work with Canadian and multinational organizations.
Grow client relationships and contribute to new opportunities, proposals and payroll solution design.
Develop high-performing teams through coaching, collaboration and clear leadership.

Skills And Attributes For Success

Strong knowledge of Canadian payroll and the end-to-end payroll lifecycle.
Understanding of global payroll and the ability to collaborate with colleagues across regions and countries to support organizations with global operations.
Deep familiarity with enterprise payroll and HRIS systems (e.g., ADP, Workday, Dayforce), multi-jurisdictional tax laws, and advanced data analytics/Excel proficiency
Experience leading complex payroll operations, implementations or managed services.
Ability to build credibility and strong relationships with senior clients.
A continuous improvement mindset and interest in payroll technology, automation and transformation.
Strong operational judgment with the ability to manage risk and resolve complex delivery challenges.
Collaborative leadership style with a focus on developing people and teams.

Qualifications

Typically, 10+ years of progressive payroll experience, including significant leadership responsibility.
A bachelor’s degree in business, accounting, finance, human resources or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
Strong knowledge of Canadian payroll requirements, processes, controls and reporting.
Experience leading payroll teams, complex implementations, client relationships or significant payroll programs.

Ideally, you’ll also have,

A PLP, PCP, CPA or other relevant professional designation.
Experience in managed payroll, outsourced payroll or a shared services environment.
Experience transitioning payroll operations to a new delivery model or provider.
Exposure to payroll technology, automation, data analytics or transformation.
Experience contributing to proposals, solution design or new client opportunities.

What We Look For

We’re looking for an experienced payroll leader who knows how to deliver payroll reliably at scale while continually looking for ways to make it better. You combine strong operational judgment with a client mindset and are comfortable leading change, solving complex delivery challenges and building strong teams. You’re also excited by the opportunity to strengthen client relationships and help grow EY’s Payroll Operate business.

What We Offer

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. In addition, our Total Rewards package allows you to decide which benefits are right for you and which ones help you create a solid foundation for your future. Our Total Rewards package includes a discretionary bonus program, a comprehensive medical, prescription drug and dental coverage plan, a defined contribution pension plan, a great vacation policy plus firm paid days that allow you to enjoy longer long weekends throughout the year, statutory holidays and paid personal days (based on province of residence), and a range of exciting programs and benefits designed to support your physical, financial and social well-being. Plus, we offer:

Support and coaching from some of the most engaging colleagues in the industry
Learning opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that’s right for you

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To help create the best experience during the recruitment process, please describe any accommodations you may need.

Inclusiveness at EY

Inclusiveness is at the heart of who we are and how we work. We’re committed to fostering an environment where differences are valued, policies and practices are equitable, and our people feel a sense of belonging. We embrace diversity and are committed to combating systemic racism, advancing gender equity and women in leadership, advocating for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, promoting our neuroinclusion and accessibility initiatives, and are dedicated to amplifying the voices of Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis) nationally as we strive towards reconciliation. Our diverse experiences, abilities, backgrounds, and perspectives make our people unique and help guide us. Because when people feel free to be their authentic selves at work, they bring their best and are empowered to build a better working world.

Learn about our commitment to Inclusiveness at https://www.ey.com/en_ca/about-us/corporate-responsibility/equity

EY | Building a better working world

EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.

At EY, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools as one element of our recruitment process to enhance efficiency and improve the candidate experience. While AI supports us in our process, human judgment and decision-making remain integral in our candidate experience. We are committed to the responsible use of AI, and our practices are continuously reviewed and refined to ensure they align with the highest ethical principles and regulatory requirements.

To all recruitment agencies: EY does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruitment agencies. Any resumes submitted without a prior agreement or request from our hiring team will not be considered. EY is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Requisition ID: 279900

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Scotiabank Enterprise Strategy group is a high-performing central team focused on designing and advancing Scotiabank’s strategic agenda
. The team works closely with the CEO, Group Heads and senior leaders to shape the Bank’s enterprise strategy and its most important business-line priorities.

Reporting to the VP, Enterprise Strategy- Canadian Banking, the Director will work closely with senior executives, business-line leaders and stakeholders across the Bank to lead complex strategy engagements, generate insights and develop recommendations that shape the Bank’s most important priorities.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be responsible for:

Strategy Projects – Must-Win Priorities

Lead a broad range of strategy engagements across the Bank, including business-line priorities and enterprise initiatives. Partner with stakeholders to structure complex problems, conduct qualitative and quantitative analysis, assess strategic and financial implications, and develop and present compelling recommendations to senior leadership.
Design and facilitate problem-solving sessions, workshops, and interviews with cross-functional stakeholders and subject matter experts to generate insights, build alignment, and advance strategic priorities.
Build alignment across business lines and corporate functions to advance strategic priorities and drive enterprise outcomes.
Partner with business-line leaders to shape strategic priorities and support the development of plans aligned to the Bank’s broader strategic objectives.
Synthesize complex findings into clear recommendations, implementation roadmaps, and governance approaches, and present them effectively to senior leaders to drive strategic outcomes.
Serve as a trusted thought partner to senior executives, helping define priorities, assess trade-offs, and navigate complex strategic decisions.
Thought Leadership

Provide thought leadership and constructive challenge on the design and advancement of strategic priorities and must-win opportunities.
Monitor emerging trends, competitive dynamics, and strategic issues to assess their implications for the Bank and its business-line strategies.
Act as a strategic counsel and thought partner for senior executives – both within the context of strategy project and on an ongoing basis
Design and support executive strategy discussions and offsites, helping senior leaders evaluate key priorities, align on strategic direction, and address emerging opportunities and challenges.
Executive Communications

Support the CEO agenda, including all-bank strategy, business line value creation projects, strategic planning, Board-level communications, and being a trusted advisor to senior leaders
Develop clear, compelling presentations and communications that translate complex strategic issues into actionable insights for senior executives, Executive Committee, and Board audiences.
In partnership with Global Communications, develop executive communications and strategic messaging that clearly articulate the Bank's priorities to internal and external stakeholders. Support the planning and delivery of key leadership, employee, and external events.
Team Leadership and Stakeholder Management

Contribute to the growth and development of the Enterprise Strategy team through recruiting, coaching, mentorship, knowledge sharing, and fostering strong partnerships across the Bank.
Ensure the Bank's risk appetite and risk culture are appropriately considered in all activities, recommendations, and decisions.
Champion a high-performance environment and implement a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops, and motivates top talent by fostering an inclusive work environment

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have the following:

MBA, PhD or relevant post-graduate degree from a recognized institution
3-4 years of experience in a top-tier management consulting firm; banking industry expertise is highly recommended
Ability to deliver results in a fast-paced, challenging, and dynamic business environment
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with ability to manage ambiguity
Superior interpersonal skills, leadership and influencing capabilities on a multi-cultural environment
Self-motivated; ability to work both independently and collaboratively with multi-functional teams
Experience running complex projects, with large group of cross-functional stakeholders
Ability to effectively manage relationships across the Bank, its partners, and external vendors
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
Collaborative and proven track record of managing and developing high-potential talent
Excellent knowledge of MS Office including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

What’s in it for you?

An inclusive & collaborative working environment that encourages creativity, curiosity, and celebrates success!
We offer a competitive rewards package: Performance bonus, Employee Share Ownership Program, and Pension Plan Matching, Health Benefits from day one!
Your career matters! You will have access to career development and progression opportunities.

Job Information

Job Title: Director Emerging Resources.

Job Requisition ID: 89476

Ministry: Energy and Minerals

Location: Edmonton or Calgary

Full or Part-Time: Full-time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Permanent

Scope: Open Competition

Closing Date: November 29, 2026

Classification: Senior Manager, Zone 2

Salary: $5,139.30 - $6,526.16 bi-weekly ($134,135 - $170,332/year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

The Ministry of Energy and Minerals is responsible for sustaining the interests of Albertans through the stewardship and responsible development of energy and mineral resource systems.

Please review Energy and Minerals to learn more and what it has to offer.

The Strategy and Market Access (SAMA) Division is responsible for developing Alberta's strategic direction to deliver on energy mandates including natural gas infrastructure development, market access, energy market diversification, strategic foresight, economic analysis, and stakeholder engagement.

The Energy Futures Branch leads the development and implementation of strategies related to natural gas infrastructure, value-add initiatives, export opportunities including liquefied natural gas (LNG) and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), critical minerals, emerging resources, and pipeline regulatory processes

The Unit of Emerging Resources is responsible for strategy development and implementation of Alberta’s critical minerals and geo-thermal resources.

Role Responsibilities

Are you a strategic thinker and collaborative leader? Energy Futures is looking for a Director, Emerging Resources to provide strategic leadership and advance Alberta’s critical minerals, geothermal energy, and other emerging resource opportunities.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Energy Futures, this position provides strategic leadership for the Department’s mandated initiatives related to critical minerals, geothermal and other emerging opportunities. The position leads professional teams responsible for strategy and legislative development, complex projects, and work across government and with external partners to advance complex policy, investment, regulatory, and market priorities.

In This Role, You Will

Provide strategic advice, analysis and recommendations, for policies, programs, and initiatives related to critical minerals, geothermal energy, and other emerging resources.
Lead strategy planning, legislative and regulatory development, implementation planning and evaluation for Alberta’s Critical Minerals Strategy and Action Plan and other emerging resource development initiatives.
Direct the preparation of decision documents, briefing notes, correspondence, cabinet and Treasury Board materials, key messages and other executive products.
Lead complex, cross-ministry and cross-jurisdictional initiatives including engagement with federal, provincial and territorial partnerships on critical minerals.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with federal counterparts and industry to advance Alberta’s interests and strategic outcomes on critical minerals and other emerging opportunities. Lead, coach, and develop managers and staff while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and results-oriented work environment.
Identify opportunities to strengthen Alberta’s competitiveness, attract investment, and support mineral exploration, development, processing, and value-added opportunities.
Direct complex policy, economic, technical, regulatory, and market analysis and provide evidence-based recommendations to senior and executive leadership.
Represent the department on intergovernmental committees, working groups, industry forums, and other strategic initiatives.
Lead unit operations, workforce planning, financial oversights, priority setting, staff development, issues management and coordination oversight and continuous improvement while managing competing priorities and emerging issues.

This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic and collaborative leader to influence Alberta’s energy and mineral future. Your leadership will help shape policies, strengthen partnerships, attract investment, and advance the responsible development of Alberta’s emerging resources.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Systems Thinking: You will consider the broader economic, regulatory, competitive, and market environment when developing strategies for critical minerals, geothermal energy, and emerging resources.
Build Collaborative Environments: You will build strategic relationships with industry, Indigenous organizations, regulators, other governments, and cross-ministry partners to advance emerging resource priorities.
Develop Self and Others: You will provide clear direction, coaching, and mentorship to managers and staff, empowering your team to deliver on complex priorities. This aligns with the APS emphasis on achieving results through others and setting clear expectations.
Creative Problem Solving: You will analyze complex policy, economic, regulatory, and market issues and develop practical, evidence-based options and recommendations for senior leadership.
Drive for Results: You will establish clear priorities and lead the delivery of high-profile strategic initiatives while balancing competing priorities and maintaining accountability for results.
Agility: You will anticipate and respond to emerging issues, changing government priorities, and evolving energy and mineral markets while providing timely strategic advice.

Qualifications

University graduation in Public Administration, Business Administration, Economics, Engineering, Science, or a related field, supplemented by seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience required in Leading complex strategic initiatives, and issues management

Related experience or education may be considered as an equivalency on a one for one basis

Assets

Knowledge of Alberta, North American and global energy landscape.
Experience with investment attraction, market development, or resource competitiveness.
Experience working with industry, Indigenous organizations, governments, regulators, international investors or other strategic partners.
Experience managing human and financial resources and leading organisational change.
Advanced writing, briefing, engagement and presentation skills.
Ability to brief and present to senior leaders and Ministers.
Demonstrated ability to develop strategies, legislation, regulations and government decision documents such as cabinet reports.
Strong policial and financial acumen.

Minimum recruitment standards outline the minimum education and experience required for appointment to a job classification.

Notes

Hours Of Work

36.25 hours per week (full time) Monday to Friday.

Term Of Employment

This is one full-time permanent position.

Location:

Petroleum Plaza Building, North Tower, Edmonton

or

AMEC Place, Calgary

Final candidates will be required to undergo a criminal records check (CRC).

Successful candidates will be required to disclose any business or financial interests, including the owning of shares or financial investments in the energy sector, to comply with the Department of Energy & Minerals’ Supplementary Code of Conduct.

Any costs associated with obtaining the required documents/checks as noted or interview travel expenses, will be the responsibility of the candidate. Out-of-province applicants can obtain the required documents/checks from the province they currently reside in.

Candidates are required to apply online. Please see Job Application Resources for more information.

In your resume, please include dates (including months and years) associated with all education and work experience. For example, January 2006 - June 2009 (part-time). This example is provided for illustrative purposes only. Applicants are encouraged to present their information clearly and thoroughly, using a format that best conveys their experience.

It is recommended applicants who have completed post-secondary studies from outside of Canada obtain an evaluation of their credentials from the International Qualifications Assessment Service (IQAS) or from a recognized Canadian Credential Evaluator; please visit the Alliance of Credential Evaluation Services of Canada for more information.

It is also recommended that applicants include the assessment certificate from IQAS or any other educational assessment service as part of their application.

new_jobs.title: Associate Director - Sponsor Coverage
new_jobs.description:
At ATB, we exist to make it possible for our clients, team members and communities. Our purpose is more than aspirational. It's a real commitment we live every day through our values (what we call the ATB ID).

About

Life at ATB is about more than work. In fact, we’re consistently recognized as one of Canada's top employers thanks to our high-care, high-performance culture, upheld by the three commitments we make to our team members:

Impact in action:
No matter where you are in the organization, you're empowered to make an impact in the lives of our clients and communities.

Thrive together:
We want you—the unique, authentic you—to feel safe and celebrated at work. We're on a continuous journey to build the most flexible and inclusive programs.

Ready for tomorrow:
We want to enable your success through interesting and challenging work, performance enablement, and learning and development.

Leadership is in our DNA at ATB, reflecting our commitment to developing world-class leaders who can truly thrive. Our Leader DNA model sets the standard for how we lead people, drive business performance, and shape a dynamic future. This is the place for purpose-driven individuals ready to deliver impactful leadership every day.

About The Team

The ATB Sponsor Coverage team is a specialized lending and coverage group focused on sponsors and the mid-market businesses they own. The team provides cash-flow-based senior lending and full capital solutions to support sponsor-led acquisitions, leveraged buyouts, recapitalizations, refinancings, growth capital and follow-on acquisitions - and then stays with those portfolio companies through the life of the investment.

Working through ATB's integrated client service model, the team partners closely with ATB Cormark Capital Markets, Investment Banking, Loan Syndications, and Financial Markets, as well as with Credit, Risk and our industry coverage teams, to deliver debt, equity, interest rate, foreign exchange and other capital solutions through one deal team.

About The Role

As ATB's next Associate Director - Sponsor Coverage, you are someone who loves solving problems and connecting with people, is client obsessed, and leverages their financial skills to find ways to create a meaningful impact on our clients. You will help deliver deep coverage of financial sponsor relationships and ensure the overall quality and credit risk of a portfolio of sponsor-backed borrowers.

You are a point of contact for clients and sponsors on senior debt and credit matters via analysis, structuring, and collaborating across multiple teams to meet client needs and ensure flawless execution. Working closely with the Senior Director, Sponsor Coverage, you will anticipate and respond to sponsor and portfolio company needs, assist with structuring competitive financing packages, and protect the quality of the portfolio at the same time.

Accountabilities

Sponsor coverage

Build and deepen relationships with sponsors, their portfolio companies, and intermediary and lender contacts, maintaining a current view of the sponsor market and of each sponsor's investment strategy, track record and active portfolio.
Assist in identifying and assessing new financing opportunities, origination and pitch activity, prepare and present financing proposals — including structure, terms and conditions, security, covenants and pricing - to sponsors and prospective clients.
Attend meetings with sponsor and portfolio company management to assess financing needs, and develop good relationships with internal stakeholders, external clients and general industry contacts.
Identify opportunities for ancillary and cross-sell business and refer or respond to them with partners in ATB Cormark Capital Markets, Investment Banking, Loan Syndications, Financial Markets and other areas of ATB.
Participate in Sales Team meetings, sharing successes, best practices, market intelligence and other information.

Transaction execution

On Each Transaction You Will Support The Senior Sales Director From First Assessment Through To Disbursement, Operating With Autonomy And Accountability, Including

Completing comprehensive due diligence on new opportunities — business, industry, financial, commercial, legal and accounting — identifying and substantiating key risks and mitigants, and completing sponsor due diligence, including investment track record, returns and alignment with capital providers.
Structuring and participating in the creation of term sheets and deal structures that solve the sponsor's and the portfolio company's current and future needs, and recommending alternative terms, conditions and covenants that make a proposal bankable within sound lending practice.
Preparation and negotiation of legal documentation including term sheets, commitment and fee letters, credit agreements and security documents in partnership with legal counsel.
Ensuring prompt follow-up for acceptance of authorizations, and reacting swiftly to problems, amendments and extensions, reporting to the Sales Director and senior management where necessary.
Overseeing disbursement of loans within authorized lending limits once credit approval, required documentation, collateral and security are in place, and coordinating closing activities with sponsors, borrowers, syndicate lenders and internal partners.
On amendment, extension and syndication transactions, support the Sales Director as a point of contact for the client and lenders, as well as managing transaction timelines end to end.

Accountabilities

Credit analysis and portfolio management

Manage a portfolio focused on the senior debt relationship with sponsor-backed clients, promoting loan growth through outstanding credit awareness and identifying opportunities to further the profitability of the portfolio.
Prepare credit assessments through completion of applications for credit, which includes analyzing financial statements and information to assess risk and determine which ATB services meet the client's needs; financial modelling and sensitivity analysis of projections; capital structure analysis with recommendations on alternate capital structures; understanding credit ratings and return assessments, with recommendations on any impact to profitability and the cost and availability of capital; and valuation and security analysis with relevant recommendations.
Develop and maintain comprehensive, company-specific financial models to evaluate cash-flow and leveraged lending scenarios, with a focus on understanding cash flows, debt capacity, leverage and debt service under base and downside cases.
Monitor the portfolio on an ongoing basis to ensure it is managed against ATB's targets: track financial covenants, borrowing conditions and internal reporting requirements, complete monitoring and control processes in a timely manner, and identify negative trends early so corrective action can be taken.
Stay abreast of current market conditions, leveraged lending trends and comparable transactions, and provide market feedback on structures and pricing to deal teams, credit officers and other internal parties.

Risk management

Demonstrate ownership and oversight with sound credit practices to mitigate and control the risks related to the portfolio, ensuring all activities are conducted in compliance with governing regulations, internal policies and procedures.
Ensure credit decisions and recommendations are in accordance with sound credit granting principles and ATB's lending policy and procedures, and maintain ATB's risk appetite, conditions of credit and documentation.

Corporate Finance Team Overview:

The Corporate Finance team within Canadian Commercial Banking, is part of BMO Financial group and covers both public and large private corporate clients operating in diversified industries. The team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Job Overview

The Associate Director plays a critical role in supporting the growth and risk‑management objectives of the portfolio. This role requires a combination of advanced financial analysis, strong credit analysis and relationship management abilities. Associate Directors contribute to client decisioning, credit structuring, and portfolio oversight, while also supporting new business development and delivering a superior client experience. Work is performed in close partnership with Managing Director and/or Director. The deal team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Analyzes credit information to support lending decisions and processes for new and existing Commercial banking loans and credit solutions in an assigned portfolio of clients. Makes credit decisions and recommendations in compliance with bank policies and procedures while maintaining an exceptional client service environment.

Negotiates loan structures and terms and conditions that align client requirements with the bank risk appetite and policies.
Assesses client repayment capacity by utilizing financial models and analytical tools to recommend appropriate loan structures and collateral requirements.
Signs off on new, renewal and extension loans within delegated authority.
Monitors portfolio to identify deteriorating credit conditions and compliance, analyses metrics, and assesses broader industry trends to spot risks and opportunities.
Evaluates portfolio performance and recommends capital allocation strategies that optimize returns with investment objectives.
Leads proposal development and delivers presentations to capture new business and expand client relationships.
Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
Develops and executes business development plans focused on enhancing client relationships and growth opportunities within the portfolio.
Builds and maintains client relationships to ensure long-term financial performance in collaboration with Relationship Manager and business partners.
Structures and supports new, renewal and extension loans aligned with client needs and bank & risk policies
Conducts financial analysis and risk assessments of clients’ credit information, for an assigned portfolio, to provide insights and make informed decisions

Minimizes BMO’s risk exposure by adhering to credit policies, regulatory standards, and operational guidelines.
Serves as a point of contact for service requests, ensuring expectations are consistently met or exceeded. Escalates issues when needed.
Supports and implements initiatives to enhance service quality, acquire new business and expand client relationships.
Identifies revenue and cross-selling opportunities to enhance portfolio growth.
Identifies share of wallet opportunities.
Leverages analysis tools to nurture and grow a portfolio that exceeds ROE thresholds and evaluates client returns on a proactive basis.
Manages timely and accurate data entry into BMO's systems and leverages the data to support decision-making.
Focus is primarily on business/group within BMO; may have broader, enterprise-wide focus.
Provides specialized consulting, analytical and technical support.
Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations.

Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.
